problems.title: Verifiable Quantum Advantage Under Adversarial Classical Challenge
problems.one_liner: Defining and certifying quantum-advantage claims that survive iterative classical counter-attacks, across sampling, OTOC, certified randomness and peaked circuits.
problems.statement: Quantum-advantage claims on pre-fault-tolerant hardware are contested almost as fast as they appear: a hardware result is announced, an independent classical algorithm (tensor-network, belief-propagation or Pauli-propagation-based) attempts to reproduce it cheaply, and the original claim is defended, narrowed or withdrawn. This happens across fundamentally different protocol families -- structured/random circuit sampling, OTOC/echo measurements, certified randomness and peaked-circuit sampling -- each with its own notion of 'verified' and no shared statistical or complexity-theoretic standard for adjudicating a claim. Solved means: a family of protocols with formal hardness proofs and matching efficient verifiers, such that a posted claim can be adjudicated -- not just asserted or informally rebutted -- against the best known classical attack within a bounded compute budget, at a scale that stays ahead of that budget as classical methods improve, ideally converging on a genuinely useful rather than merely hard-to-simulate computation.

anchors.item: Quantum advantage by end of 2026 target; Nighthawk processor (120 qubits, 7,500 gates in 2026)
anchors.dependency: Needs a verification/adjudication method that survives classical rebuttal, not just a hard-to-simulate circuit.

anchors.item: Open Quantum Advantage Tracker launched Nov 2025 with Algorithmiq, Flatiron Institute and BlueQubit
anchors.dependency: Needs a standing classical-challenge process to make advantage claims falsifiable and adjudicable.

anchors.item: 'Verifiable quantum advantage' via Quantum Echoes/OTOC (Nature, Oct 2025): 65 qubits, ~13,000x vs Frontier
anchors.dependency: Needs an independent, reproducible verification protocol beyond company-reported classical-cost estimates.

anchors.item: Grand Challenge of Quantum Applications: no application has yet reached Stage V
anchors.dependency: A verified 'useful, beyond-classical' computation needs the same certification tools as pure advantage claims.

anchors.item: 48-logical-qubit IQP sampling demonstration (2023)
anchors.dependency: Baseline logical-qubit sampling result that would need a verifiable-advantage protocol layered on top.

criteria_why.C1: Requires new verification protocols and complexity-theoretic hardness proofs, not just bigger circuits.
criteria_why.C2: Fidelity/XEB scores, certified-entropy bits and classical-runtime-to-match are directly computable per claim.
criteria_why.C3: Open tracker data and published circuits let any group attempt a classical attack without owning hardware.
criteria_why.C4: Sampling, OTOC, certified-randomness and peaked-circuit protocols use different, incompatible verification definitions today.
criteria_why.C5: Splits naturally from defining metrics, to first demonstrations, to adversarial scale-up, to formal guarantees.
criteria_why.C6: Peaked-circuit lower bounds and unstructured proofs of quantumness require genuinely hard complexity theory.

problems.access_note: Attacking claims needs HPC-scale classical compute (Fugaku-class, multi-ExaFLOP); raw claim data is often public via trackers.

metrics.name: Cross-entropy benchmarking (XEB) fidelity
metrics.def: Normalized log-likelihood of measured bitstrings under the ideal circuit's output distribution (dimensionless, 0-1).
metrics.sota: Fidelity lower bound 0.284 (95% CI), IBM/UChicago doped-Clifford, 97 qubits, July 2026

metrics.name: Classical compute needed to match a claim
metrics.def: Node-hours or aggregate FLOPs the best known classical algorithm needs to reproduce a quantum output at the claimed fidelity.
metrics.sota: 12,888 Fugaku nodes reach 51 qubits before diverging vs. a 74-qubit quantum claim, Qedma/RIKEN/BlueQubit, July 2026

metrics.name: Certified min-entropy per protocol run
metrics.def: Bits of randomness certified against a computational-hardness assumption via classical spot-checking of quantum-generated samples.
metrics.sota: 71,313 certified bits, Quantinuum H2 (56 qubits), verified with 1.1 ExaFLOPS aggregate, March 2025

metrics.name: Peaked-circuit heavy-output probability
metrics.def: Probability mass concentrated on the single 'heavy' bitstring output; must exceed 1/poly(n) for efficient verification.
metrics.sota: Still largely theoretical/simulation-scale; 2026 work shows some heuristic constructions are classically simulable

stages.name: Definitions and baseline classical simulators
stages.goal: Establish formal advantage definitions and open, reusable classical-baseline tooling.
stages.exit: Published framework paper plus a public standing tracker/challenge platform.
stages.note: IBM/Pasqal framework (2025) and IBM's open tracker (2025) both live.

stages.name: First verifiable-ish demonstrations with partial classical crosscheck
stages.goal: Hardware results at 50-130-qubit scale with at least one independent classical cross-check attempt.
stages.exit: Published Nature/Science-tier claim plus an independent classical rebuttal within about a year.
stages.note: IBM utility experiment (2023), its two rebuttals, certified randomness (2025), D-Wave/Flatiron dispute (2025).

stages.name: Roadmap-scale adversarial cycle (2026)
stages.goal: Claims at 56-97+ qubits posted for open challenge, with rebuttals arriving within weeks.
stages.exit: A posted claim survives at least two independent classical-attack attempts at full roadmap scale.
stages.note: Three IBM-linked claims (July 2026) plus one partial classical rebuttal (Oh); cycle still unresolved.

stages.name: Peaked-circuit and complexity-theoretic verification maturation
stages.goal: Efficient verifiable protocols backed by formal hardness proofs and demonstrated peakedness at useful scale.
stages.exit: A peaked-circuit-style construction resists best-known classical spoofing at >=50 qubits with a formal reduction.
stages.note: Foundational proofs exist (2022-2024); 2026 work shows some heuristic constructions are classically simulable after all.

stages.name: Community-adjudicated standard and a useful beyond-classical computation
stages.goal: Cross-company/academia agreed adjudication process; first genuinely useful computation verified this way.
stages.exit: An application reaches Google's Grand-Challenge 'Stage V' bar under a community-vetted verification protocol.
stages.note: No application at Stage V yet; 2026 survey names fault-tolerant QEC as the real remaining gap.

IBM.headline: Three 2026 hardware claims posted openly for classical challenge
IBM.summary: IBM launched an open Quantum Advantage Tracker (Nov 2025, with Algorithmiq, Flatiron and BlueQubit) and in July 2026 posted three claims for challenge: a doped-Clifford sampling result on 97 qubits (70 data + 27 syndrome ancillas) (fidelity lower bound 0.284), a 74-qubit Floquet-Ising result (arXiv 2607.24937) and a 56-qubit Loschmidt-echo result with Algorithmiq. Its own IBM/Pasqal paper (2025) proposes a platform-agnostic advantage definition.

Google.headline: Quantum Echoes claim (65 qubits) plus RCS verification theory
Google.summary: Google reported a 'verifiable quantum advantage' via the OTOC-based Quantum Echoes algorithm on Willow (Nature, Oct 2025; 65 qubits, ~13,000x vs. a Frontier estimate), reproduced across two chips. Its earlier Nature 2024 paper on phase transitions in random circuit sampling maps when XEB-based verification remains reliable as noise and size scale, underpinning the verification side of its claims.

QuEra.headline: 2023 logical-qubit IQP sampling remains the reference result
QuEra.summary: QuEra/Harvard's 2023 demonstration used 48 logical qubits for IQP-type sampling on reconfigurable neutral-atom arrays, an error-corrected rather than error-mitigated route toward hard-to-simulate output. No comparable 2025-2026 QuEra verifiable-advantage paper or classical-rebuttal exchange was identified in this review; public emphasis has stayed on logical-qubit scaling and fault-tolerance roadmap milestones rather than on posting adversarial advantage claims for open classical challenge the way IBM and Google have.

IonQ.headline: No public IonQ work on certifying beyond-classical results found.
IonQ.summary: No IonQ-authored protocol, experiment or analysis from 2022 to September 2026 certifies a beyond-classical computation against classical counter-attack. IonQ's application announcements are performance or workflow demonstrations rather than certified-advantage claims, and its roadmap targets fault-tolerant scale rather than verifiable advantage, so the problem is open on IonQ's side.
IonQ.gateWhy: IonQ's published roadmap does not list certified or verifiable advantage as a milestone.

Community.headline: Very active: independent groups match or rebut most claims within months
Community.summary: Tindall et al. and Begušić & Chan matched IBM's 2023 utility experiment with tensor-network methods within a year; the Flatiron Institute's belief-propagation tensor networks challenged D-Wave's 2025 annealing claim; Oh's 2026 'frozen-tree' algorithm targets sampling-based verification loopholes; Aaronson & Zhang (UT Austin) and 2026 follow-ups probe peaked-circuit hardness and its classical-simulability limits; Yamakawa & Zhandry supply complexity-theoretic foundations; Ryan LaRose's 2026 review (Michigan State) synthesizes the full claim/rebuttal history.

overall.headline: Mid-adversarial-cycle: 2026 claims posted, rebuttals arriving in weeks
overall.summary: The field is mid-cycle on its most roadmap-relevant claims yet: three IBM-linked demonstrations (56-97 qubits) went up for open challenge in July 2026 alongside Google's 65-qubit Quantum Echoes result, with at least one partial classical rebuttal already posted. No unified verification standard exists across protocol families, and Google's own Grand Challenge paper states no application has reached its Stage V bar.

gaps.gap: No unified verification standard across sampling, OTOC, randomness and peaked-circuit protocols
gaps.why_hard: Each protocol has different threat models and assumptions; unifying them needs new complexity theory bridging noise, verifier cost and hardness.
gaps.entry_point: Formalize a common verifier-cost-vs-prover-cost framework spanning the four protocol families, starting from the IBM/Pasqal definition.

gaps.gap: Classical attacks lag hardware scale-up by only weeks, not years, at roadmap scale
gaps.why_hard: Scaling tensor-network/Pauli-propagation methods requires new approximation theory plus HPC engineering to track each new claim.
gaps.entry_point: Use IBM's open tracker datasets to benchmark successive classical-algorithm improvements against a fixed claim over time.

gaps.gap: No neutral, timed adjudication process; claims and rebuttals are self-published and PR-driven
gaps.why_hard: Requires community governance and agreed timelines, not just new algorithms or proofs.
gaps.entry_point: Extend the tracker model (open data plus a challenge window) to Google's and QuEra's claims with third-party adjudicators.

problems.note: Claims and rebuttals now cycle in weeks. IBM's July 2026 doped-Clifford result drew a 'frozen-tree' classical preprint within days, though its author says it does not directly refute the structured task.

problems.title: Certified Error Bars for HPC-Coupled Quantum Algorithms
problems.one_liner: Giving quantum-centric-supercomputing methods (SQD/SKQD, operator backpropagation, mitigation) rigorous, scalable accuracy guarantees, not just empirical validation.
problems.statement: Sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD/SKQD), operator backpropagation, multi-product Hamiltonian simulation, circuit cutting, and error-mitigation techniques (PEC, ZNE, tensor-network mitigation) let quantum-centric supercomputers tackle chemistry and materials problems beyond exact-diagonalization scale, but their accuracy is mostly validated empirically -- against small known systems, or via internal consistency -- rather than through rigorous, general error bounds. Meanwhile complexity theory shows worst-case error-mitigation sampling overhead is exponential in circuit volume, and independent critiques have found concrete failure modes (configuration-recovery breakdown under noise) in SQD-family methods on realistic hardware. Solved means: a theory that predicts, before running an experiment, the accuracy achievable at a given qubit count, noise level and classical post-processing budget, with a provable, non-heuristic bound, for at least one HPC-coupled method family -- tight enough to certify a claimed result correct to within a stated error versus ground truth, not just plausible relative to other heuristics.

anchors.item: Nighthawk processor targeting quantum advantage by end of 2026 (120 qubits, 7,500 gates)
anchors.dependency: SQD/SKQD and error-mitigated algorithms are IBM's main path to a 2026 utility/advantage claim beyond raw sampling.

anchors.item: IBM/RIKEN quantum-centric supercomputing: System Two co-located with Fugaku, enabling 77-qubit SQD
anchors.dependency: HPC-coupled algorithms need this classical-compute-adjacent hardware to scale past exact-diagonalization limits.

anchors.item: Grand Challenge of Quantum Applications: no application has yet reached Stage V
anchors.dependency: Error-mitigated HPC-coupled algorithms are a main candidate route to a Stage-V-qualifying application.

anchors.item: 48-logical-qubit IQP sampling (2023)
anchors.dependency: Neutral-atom error-corrected route is an alternative to error-mitigated HPC-coupling for the same accuracy goal.

criteria_why.C1: Provable convergence, tight error bounds and new mitigation theory are original research, not engineering.
criteria_why.C2: Energy error vs. exact/FCI benchmarks and sampling overhead are precise, directly computable metrics.
criteria_why.C3: Open Qiskit addons (SQD, OBP, Pauli propagation) let any group extend or critique the methods.
criteria_why.C4: No single accepted framework yet unifies rigorous error bars across SQD, PEC, OBP and MPF.
criteria_why.C5: Splits from tooling, to first HPC-scale demos, to failure-mode critiques, to provable bounds, to unification.
criteria_why.C6: Proving tight, non-exponential convergence against proven worst-case exponential mitigation limits is hard theory.

problems.access_note: Needs IBM Quantum cloud access plus HPC (Fugaku-class) for the classical diagonalization/mitigation post-processing.

metrics.name: Ground-state energy error vs. exact/FCI reference
metrics.def: Absolute energy difference |E_method - E_exact| in Hartree for a benchmark molecule or lattice model.
metrics.sota: SQD within chemical-accuracy range for N2 active space; 77-qubit [4Fe-4S] cluster result, IBM/RIKEN, 2025

metrics.name: Sampling/shot overhead for error mitigation
metrics.def: Number of circuit executions (or effective variance amplification) needed to reach target accuracy vs. noiseless.
metrics.sota: Proven exponential in circuit volume in general (Takagi et al. 2022), tightened further by Quek et al. 2024

metrics.name: Configuration-recovery accuracy under noise
metrics.def: Fraction of correct electronic configurations recovered by SQD/SKQD's classical diagonalization step at a given noise level.
metrics.sota: Characterized as a concrete failure mode by the 2025 Critical Limitations paper and a 2026 noise-impact follow-up

metrics.name: Classical reconstruction overhead for circuit cutting
metrics.def: Multiplicative sampling overhead as a function of number of cut wires/gates needed to reconstruct the full-circuit output.
metrics.sota: Exponential in naive cutting; improved by a 2026 combined gate-and-wire-cut framework (TUM)

stages.exit: Public tool release plus a peer-reviewed method paper for at least one technique.

stages.goal: Show quantum-sampled ansatz plus classical diagonalization solving problems beyond brute-force exact methods.

stages.note: SQD reached 77 qubits on [4Fe-4S] (2025); sparse Pauli-Lindblad PEC and randomized MPF both published 2022-2023.

stages.name: Rigor stage: exposing failure modes and tightening bounds
stages.goal: Characterize when and why these methods fail or lose accuracy; tighten error-mitigation lower bounds.
stages.exit: Peer-reviewed critique-and-response cycle establishing accuracy-regime boundaries.
stages.note: Critical Limitations (2025) and a 2026 noise-impact follow-up found concrete SQD failure modes; Quek et al. tightened EM limits.

stages.name: Provable, certified error bars at roadmap scale
stages.goal: Rigorous, non-heuristic accuracy guarantees for HPC-coupled algorithms at 2026-2027 roadmap qubit counts.
stages.exit: Peer-reviewed convergence proof or error bound validated against an exact benchmark at roadmap-relevant scale.
stages.note: IBM's 'provable convergence' SKQD work (2026) and MPF commutator-scaling bounds (2026) are early steps, not yet general.

stages.name: Unified cost-accounting framework and roadmap integration
stages.goal: Single framework comparing total classical-plus-quantum cost across SQD/PEC/MPF/cutting against classical baselines.
stages.exit: Community-adopted benchmark suite reporting cross-technique total cost vs. accuracy on shared instances.
stages.note: No cross-technique benchmark suite found; each method family is still evaluated on its own separate benchmarks.

IBM.headline: SQD/SKQD plus Qiskit mitigation addons, HPC-coupled via Fugaku
IBM.summary: IBM's SQD reached 77 qubits on a [4Fe-4S] cluster (Science Advances, 2025) via Heron+Fugaku; sparse Pauli-Lindblad PEC (Nature Physics, 2023) and its 2024 noise-learning follow-up underpin practical error cancellation; 2025-2026 work targets improved and 'provably convergent' SKQD, and operator backpropagation was improved in 2025. All are released as open Qiskit addons, with System Two/RIKEN providing the HPC coupling.

Google.headline: No SQD- or PEC-style work identified; effort centers on verifiable advantage
Google.summary: No Google paper on sample-based diagonalization, operator backpropagation or Pauli-Lindblad-style error cancellation was identified in this review. Google's pre-fault-tolerant work concentrates on verifiable advantage (Quantum Echoes, covered under P01) rather than HPC-coupled algorithms with certified error bars.

QuEra.headline: No public SQD/PEC/OBP-style work found; different error-suppression approach
QuEra.summary: Neutral-atom systems use physically distinct error-suppression strategies (e.g., erasure conversion, reconfigurable-array logical encoding) rather than the gate-based probabilistic error cancellation, Pauli-Lindblad noise learning, or classical-diagonalization post-processing this problem covers. No QuEra publication matching the SQD/SKQD/OBP/multi-product-formula/circuit-cutting bundle was identified in this review, and its HPC-coupling and certified-accuracy work, if any exists, was not found here.

IonQ.headline: Only empirical error mitigation (debiasing) documented; no certified error bars published.
IonQ.summary: IonQ's cloud documentation describes compiler-level debiasing, which runs symmetric circuit variants (at least 500 shots split into 25 executions), and an optional sharpening step that applies plurality voting. The documentation provides no error bars, confidence intervals or certified accuracy guarantees, and warns that sharpening can distort probability distributions. No IonQ paper found gives rigorous accuracy guarantees for sample-based diagonalization or other pre-fault-tolerant hybrid methods, so the problem is not addressed beyond empirical mitigation.
IonQ.gateWhy: IonQ's roadmap is built on fault-tolerant logical qubits and does not depend on certified pre-fault-tolerant hybrid methods.

Community.headline: Active critique-and-extend ecosystem tightening bounds rather than overturning claims
Community.summary: Academic groups published concrete failure-mode critiques of SQD/QSCI (a 2025 Critical Limitations paper and a 2026 noise-impact follow-up), tightened the complexity-theoretic limits on error-mitigation overhead (Takagi et al. 2022; Quek et al., Nature Physics 2024), refined multi-product-formula error bounds (Faehrmann et al.; a 2026 commutator-scaling follow-up), and built more scalable circuit-cutting frameworks (a 2026 TUM combined gate-and-wire-cut framework), alongside Algorithmiq's commercially deployed tensor-network error mitigation.

overall.headline: SQD/SKQD demonstrated at 77+ qubits; rigorous error bars still emerging
overall.summary: HPC-coupled methods (SQD/SKQD, PEC, OBP, MPF, circuit cutting) are all past their first demonstration stage, with IBM's 77-qubit SQD result on a [4Fe-4S] cluster the clearest roadmap-relevant milestone. The literature has moved into a rigor stage: independent critiques (2025-2026) have found concrete SQD failure modes and complexity theory has tightened worst-case mitigation-overhead bounds, but provable, roadmap-scale error certification remains open, and IBM's own 'provable convergence' work is still at an early, conference-presentation stage rather than a published proof.

gaps.gap: No method combines HPC-scale SQD-type accuracy with a provable, non-exponential error bound
gaps.why_hard: Rigorous bounds for classically-hard sampling-based methods need new statistical/complexity theory bridging quantum sampling noise and classical post-processing error.
gaps.entry_point: Extend IBM's 2026 'provable convergence' SKQD line to full peer-reviewed proofs on benchmarks beyond N2/[4Fe-4S].

gaps.gap: Proven exponential mitigation overhead versus claimed practical scalability of SQD/OBP/TEM are unreconciled
gaps.why_hard: Reconciling worst-case exponential lower bounds with typical-case performance needs a theory of which real Hamiltonians avoid the worst case.
gaps.entry_point: Characterize structured-Hamiltonian classes (low entanglement, sparse Pauli weight) where mitigation overhead is provably sub-exponential.

gaps.gap: No shared cost-accounting framework compares cutting, MPF, PEC and SQD against one classical baseline
gaps.why_hard: Needs a common cost model across techniques with very different quantum/classical cost trade-offs, combined in real pipelines.
gaps.entry_point: Build an open benchmark suite, extending existing Qiskit addons, reporting total cost-to-target-accuracy across techniques on shared instances.

problems.note: Critiques here (limits of quantum-selected CI, exponential mitigation-overhead bounds) refine claims rather than overturn them, so progress reads as a tightening of guarantees.
problems.name: Certified error bars

doe.pullWhy: Pre-fault-tolerant. Two of the report's state-of-the-art examples, protein-ligand complexes and fusion-blanket molten salts, rely on sample-based diagonalization, but no logical-qubit tier depends on these methods.
doe.verifyWhy: Results are checked against exact diagonalization, coupled cluster or neutron-scattering data, as DOE's science roadmap asks.
doe.vv: Energy error against exact or experimental references; sampling overhead.

problems.title: Real-time decoding for qLDPC codes and logical circuits
problems.one_liner: Building decoders that hit hard latency, throughput and accuracy targets for qLDPC memories and correlated logical operations under circuit-level noise, on a shared benchmark.
problems.statement: Real-time decoding must keep pace with the syndrome-extraction cycle so backlog never grows: for surface codes this means roughly 1 microsecond per cycle at large distance, and for qLDPC codes syndromes must be decoded fast enough for lattice surgery, qLDPC surgery/extractor rounds, and correlated decoding of transversal gates, under realistic circuit-level noise rather than idealized code-capacity models. 'Solved' means demonstrating, at roadmap-relevant scale (IBM Starling's ~200 logical qubits/1e8 gates, QuEra Libra's >256 logical qubits at 1e-6 logical error), a decoder or decoder family spanning matching, BP-based, search-based and neural approaches that simultaneously meets a hard per-cycle latency deadline on real FPGA/ASIC/GPU hardware, sustains throughput without backlog via windowing, preserves near-optimal logical error suppression relative to offline decoding, and handles the correlated, non-independent syndromes produced by transversal and lattice-surgery operations, with results reported on a common, reproducible benchmark comparable across vendors and code families.

anchors.item: Kookaburra (2026): first qLDPC memory + logical processing unit module
anchors.dependency: Module requires a real-time qLDPC decoder meeting the module's cycle-time budget

anchors.item: Starling (2029): 200 logical qubits, 1e8 gates
anchors.dependency: Needs real-time qLDPC decoding sustained across 1e8 gates without backlog

anchors.item: Willow: real-time decoding of d=5 surface code, 63 microsecond average latency, 1.1 microsecond cycles
anchors.dependency: Sets the demonstrated latency baseline that qLDPC and correlated decoders must match at larger scale

anchors.item: Libra (2028): >256 logical qubits at 1e-6 logical error
anchors.dependency: Cites fast decoding with NVIDIA; neutral-atom transversal gates need correlated decoding integrated in time

criteria_why.C1: No decoder provably meets joint latency+accuracy targets for general qLDPC under circuit-level noise
criteria_why.C2: Logical error rate, decode latency (ns/µs per cycle), and throughput are directly measurable in sim and hardware
criteria_why.C3: Open decoders and simulators (Stim, PyMatching, Tesseract, BP+OSD) let anyone benchmark new codes/decoders
criteria_why.C4: Matching, BP, search and neural decoder families coexist with no single theory unifying their tradeoffs
criteria_why.C5: Clear path: simulation to FPGA/GPU, memory to logical ops, single-patch to correlated/windowed decoding
criteria_why.C6: General qLDPC decoding is NP-hard; latency-accuracy guarantees under circuit noise remain unproven

problems.access_note: Decoder algorithms are developed/benchmarked via Stim/PyMatching simulation; hardware validation needs vendor lab access

metrics.name: Decoding latency per cycle
metrics.def: Wall-clock time per syndrome-extraction round the decoder must not exceed to avoid backlog, on target hardware, in ns/µs
metrics.sota: 63 µs average (1.1 µs cycles) on Google Willow d=5 hardware (2024); AlphaQubit 2 claims <1 µs/cycle to d=11 surface / d=9 color on accelerators in simulation (Google, 2025)

metrics.name: Logical-error suppression vs. offline decoding
metrics.def: Ratio of a real-time decoder's logical error rate to that of an optimal offline decoder (MWPM/BP+OSD with unlimited time) at fixed physical error rate
metrics.sota: Relay-BP matches MWPM on surface codes and beats BP+OSD+CS-10 on bivariate-bicycle codes (IBM, 2025); Tesseract gives 14-19x logical-error suppression vs. surface code on the [[144,12,12]] BB code, vs ~10x for BP+OSD/correlated matching (Google, 2025)

metrics.name: qLDPC decoder speedup vs. BP-OSD baseline
metrics.def: Wall-clock decode time relative to the BP-OSD industry-standard baseline at matched accuracy
metrics.sota: Ambiguity Clustering reports up to 27-150x speedup over BP-OSD (Riverlane, 2024)

metrics.name: Backlog-free scaling
metrics.def: Whether mean decode time per round stays below cycle time as code distance/qubit count grows
metrics.sota: Parallel/sliding-window schemes show no backlog growth in simulation to large lattice sizes (Skoric et al., 2023); single-CPU real-time decoding simulated backlog-free to 408 logical qubits (IonQ, 2026)

stages.note: Willow (2024) and FPGA MWPM accelerators demonstrate this for surface codes

stages.name: Real-time qLDPC decoding: algorithms and FPGA implementations
stages.goal: Extend real-time decoding from surface codes to qLDPC memories (e.g. bivariate-bicycle, gross code)
stages.exit: FPGA/ASIC decoder meets cycle-time deadline on a qLDPC memory at rate-relevant block length
stages.note: Relay-BP and gross-code FPGA decoding are 2025 first steps; only small qLDPC blocks demonstrated

stages.name: Backlog-free scaling via windowing
stages.goal: Keep decode time bounded as distance/qubit count grows using parallel/sliding windows
stages.exit: Demonstrated (in hardware or realistic simulation) no backlog growth at roadmap-relevant qubit counts
stages.note: Windowing theory is mature for surface codes; qLDPC and neural-decoder windowing are early

stages.name: Correlated decoding of composite logical operations
stages.goal: Decode lattice surgery, qLDPC surgery/extractors and transversal gates jointly rather than per-patch
stages.exit: Correlated decoder demonstrated on a multi-patch transversal circuit with measured logical-error improvement over independent decoding
stages.note: Cain et al. and its 2025 speedup are simulation-only, for neutral-atom transversal algorithms

stages.name: Unified, at-scale, cross-vendor real-time decoding
stages.goal: One benchmark and decoder family meeting latency+accuracy+scale targets across codes and hardware vendors
stages.exit: Common benchmark adopted by 2+ vendors reporting latency/throughput/accuracy for the same qLDPC workload
stages.note: No shared benchmark exists yet; AlphaQubit 2's scale claims are simulation-only

IBM.headline: Relay-BP plus FPGA demo bring real-time decoding to qLDPC gross-code memories (2025)
IBM.summary: IBM's Relay-BP (2025) modifies belief propagation with disordered memory strengths, matching MWPM accuracy on surface codes and beating BP+OSD+CS-10 on bivariate-bicycle codes, explicitly designed for FPGA/ASIC implementation. A companion 2025 paper reports real-time FPGA decoding of the [[144,12,12]] gross-code memory on AMD hardware. This ties directly to Kookaburra (2026) and Starling (2029), both requiring real-time qLDPC decoding; no correlated-decoding or transversal-gate results have appeared yet.

Google.headline: Willow proved real-time hardware decoding; Tesseract and AlphaQubit 2 push accuracy/speed in simulation
Google.summary: Google's Willow processor (Nature, 2024) ran real-time decoding at distance 5 with 1.1 µs cycles and 63 µs average latency on classical hardware beside the chip. Google Quantum AI's Tesseract (2025) is an open-source A*-search decoder reaching near-optimal accuracy faster than BP+OSD/correlated matching. AlphaQubit 2 (Bausch et al., Dec 2025) claims sub-1 µs/cycle neural decoding to d=11 (surface) and d=9 (color) on commercial accelerators, but only in simulation so far.

QuEra.headline: Correlated-decoding theory for transversal neutral-atom algorithms; roadmap ties fast decoding to NVIDIA
QuEra.summary: QuEra/Harvard theorists (Cain et al., PRL 2024) introduced correlated decoding for transversal-gate logical algorithms on neutral atoms, with a 2025 follow-up improving speed; both remain simulation-based. QuEra's Libra roadmap (2028, >256 logical qubits at 1e-6) cites 'fast decoding enabling real-time error correction' developed with NVIDIA, but no public real-time hardware decoding result for QuEra's own platform has appeared yet.

IonQ.headline: Beam-search qLDPC decoders benchmarked in software on simulated data; no live hardware decoding.
IonQ.summary: IonQ authors published a beam-search decoder for quantum LDPC codes (December 2025) that, in circuit-level simulation, cuts logical error up to 17x versus BP-OSD or runs 26x faster at equal accuracy, with 99.9th-percentile runtime under 1 ms per round on one CPU core. A 2026 follow-up decodes simulated streams for 102 to 408 logical qubits on one Apple M4 Max CPU with under 12% slowdown. A soft-output variant was tried on IonQ trapped-ion data. Real-time decoding of live hardware syndromes is not reported.
IonQ.gateWhy: Real-time decoding binds once 100+ logical qubits run 10^5 hard operations; smaller prototype runs can tolerate slow or offline decoding.

Community.headline: Dense open ecosystem of FPGA/GPU matching, BP and neural decoders outside the three roadmap vendors
Community.summary: Academic and industry groups drive most real-time decoding infrastructure: Riverlane's Ambiguity Clustering (2024) and Localized Statistics Decoding (2024) speed up qLDPC decoding; Micro Blossom and FPGA sparse-blossom (QASBA) accelerate matching. GARI and DART-Q (2026) target scalable/deadline-driven FPGA qLDPC decoding, and machine-learning decoders now target bivariate-bicycle codes under circuit-level noise. IonQ showed single-CPU real-time decoding is feasible in simulation to 408 logical qubits (2026), and Battistel et al.'s 2023 survey remains the field's reference framing.

overall.headline: Surface-code real-time decoding is solved on hardware; qLDPC and correlated decoding are still maturing
overall.summary: Real-time decoding of surface-code memories is demonstrated on hardware (Google Willow) with sub-100-µs latency and no reported backlog. Extending this to qLDPC codes at roadmap scale (IBM Kookaburra/Starling, QuEra Libra) is progressing via Relay-BP, FPGA gross-code decoding, GARI and DART-Q, but hardware demonstrations remain small-scale. Correlated decoding for lattice surgery and transversal operations is largely simulation-only. A common cross-vendor benchmark spanning latency, throughput and accuracy under circuit-level noise does not yet exist, and learned or search-based decoders (AlphaQubit, Tesseract) have been evaluated offline, not inside a hardware feedback loop.

gaps.gap: No common cross-decoder, cross-code real-time benchmark
gaps.why_hard: Latency depends on code, noise model, hardware target and windowing scheme, so published results use incompatible metrics
gaps.entry_point: Extend qec-lego-bench or QEC Explorer to report latency/throughput/accuracy under one shared circuit-level noise model and hardware budget

gaps.gap: Correlated decoding for transversal gates combined with qLDPC lattice surgery
gaps.why_hard: Correlated syndromes from transversal gates plus non-local qLDPC checks jointly break the locality assumptions most fast decoders rely on
gaps.entry_point: Extend Cain et al.'s correlated-decoding framework to bivariate-bicycle qLDPC lattice-surgery/extractor circuits in simulation

gaps.gap: Hardware-verified windowed decoding at qLDPC roadmap scale
gaps.why_hard: Sliding/parallel windows are proven for surface codes but not yet demonstrated on FPGA/ASIC for qLDPC at Starling/Libra-scale distances
gaps.entry_point: Port an existing sliding-window scheme (Skoric et al.) to a gross-code or bivariate-bicycle FPGA pipeline and measure backlog growth

problems.note: AlphaQubit 2 and Tesseract results are simulation or offline. On real hardware, only surface-code decoding (Willow) and FPGA qLDPC decoding (IBM with AMD) are confirmed.
problems.name: Real-time qLDPC decoding

doe.pullWhy: IBM's qLDPC modules need it before any logical operation; QuEra's high-rate codes, IonQ's 800-logical-qubit chip and Google's 100-logical-qubit lattice surgery need fast, often correlated decoding at First-generation scale.
doe.verifyWhy: Latency and logical error under live decoding are what DOE's V&V testbed measures as classical control stack integration.
doe.vv: Decoder latency and logical error with live decoding.

problems.title: Decoder-controller co-design and end-to-end feedback guarantees
problems.one_liner: Co-designing the measurement-to-correction control loop and proving its end-to-end latency, throughput and correctness hold as codes, decoders and scale change.
problems.statement: The real-time QEC control loop -- measurement, classification, transport to classical hardware, decoding, Pauli-frame update, and conditional operation -- must meet a hard latency budget (roughly the code's cycle time: about 1 microsecond for superconducting surface codes, tens of microseconds tolerance for neutral atoms/trapped ions) without backlog, across heterogeneous FPGA/GPU/ASIC hardware, and as codes and decoders change. 'Solved' means a documented controller-decoder interface (data formats, timing contracts, backpressure handling) with formally stated and ideally verified guarantees on end-to-end latency and Pauli-frame correctness; demonstrated hardware integration of a full loop at scale (hundreds of qubits, thousands of rounds) without backlog growth; and a design methodology usable across control-hardware vendors (superconducting, neutral-atom, trapped-ion) and decoder families (matching, BP, neural) rather than a bespoke integration per vendor. It also covers feedforward timing for non-Clifford operations such as magic-state injection, where classical latency directly gates the logical clock speed.

anchors.item: Starling (2029): 200 logical qubits, 1e8 gates
anchors.dependency: Requires a controller-decoder loop sustaining real-time qLDPC decoding across 1e8 gates without backlog

anchors.item: Libra (2028): >256 logical qubits at 1e-6 logical error
anchors.dependency: Cites fast decoding with NVIDIA; needs correlated decoding integrated into the control loop in time for transversal gates

anchors.item: Willow real-time control loop (d=5, 63 µs avg latency, 1.1 µs cycles); RSA-cryptanalysis estimate assumes a 10 µs reaction-time budget
anchors.dependency: Sets the demonstrated latency budget that controller-decoder co-design must hit as codes/decoders scale

criteria_why.C1: No general theory gives end-to-end latency/correctness guarantees as codes and decoders change
criteria_why.C2: Round-trip latency, throughput and backlog growth are directly measurable on real control hardware
criteria_why.C3: Open stacks (QubiC, NVQLink, RISC-Q) enable contributions, but real control hardware access is limited
criteria_why.C4: Each vendor (Riverlane/Qblox, NVIDIA/NVQLink, Quantinuum) uses a bespoke interface; no shared standard exists
criteria_why.C5: Clear progression: single-vendor loop to standardized interface to verified guarantees at scale
criteria_why.C6: Formally verifying timing/correctness across changing decoders and codes is largely unsolved

problems.access_note: Full-loop demonstrations need real control electronics (FPGA/ASIC/GPU + QPU); interface/protocol design and verification work is simulation-only

metrics.name: End-to-end round-trip latency
metrics.def: Time from the last relevant syndrome sample to an applied Pauli-frame/gate correction, measured on real control hardware, in µs
metrics.sota: 9.6 µs over 9 rounds, mean <1 µs/round (Rigetti+Riverlane, Caune et al., 2024); 6.9 µs (Surface-17) to <12 µs (Surface-161) closed loop (Qblox+Riverlane, 2026); 3.96 µs max round-trip demonstrated for NVQLink (NVIDIA, 2025)

metrics.name: Decoding-feedback latency at scale
metrics.def: End-to-end decode-plus-feedback latency as a function of code distance/qubit count
metrics.sota: 446 ns demonstrated at distance-3; sub-microsecond projected to distance-21 (~881 physical qubits) (Liu, Lee, Xu, Huang, Wu, 2026)

metrics.name: Backlog-free throughput
metrics.def: Whether the decoder-plus-controller loop sustains code-cycle-rate throughput indefinitely without a growing queue of undecoded rounds
metrics.sota: No backlog reported to d=5 on live hardware (Google Willow, 2024); backlog-free single-CPU decoding simulated to 408 logical qubits (IonQ, 2026)

infra.what: Open-source FPGA-based control and measurement system for superconducting qubits

infra.what: Real-time QEC control-decoder interface and protocol, integrated with Qblox control hardware

stages.name: Open control-stack infrastructure
stages.goal: Open-source FPGA control/measurement systems and control SoC generators as a shared foundation
stages.exit: Open-source control stack adopted by multiple research groups beyond its authors
stages.note: QubiC (2021) and RISC-Q (DAC 2026) provide reusable open control hardware/software

stages.name: First real-time hardware control loops (single vendor, single code)
stages.goal: Close the full measurement-to-correction loop on live hardware for one code and one vendor stack
stages.exit: Sustained real-time decode-and-correct demonstrated on a physical QPU with reported latency numbers
stages.note: Caune et al. (Rigetti+Riverlane) and Google Willow are the first public full-loop demonstrations

stages.name: Cross-vendor controller-decoder interfaces
stages.goal: Standardize the controller-decoder interface so decoders and control hardware from different vendors interoperate
stages.exit: An interface (e.g. NVQLink, QECi) adopted by 2+ independent hardware vendors
stages.note: NVQLink already has 17 hardware partners and 9 national labs; QECi links Riverlane decoders to Qblox controllers

stages.name: Scaling the loop toward roadmap size
stages.goal: Push end-to-end latency and backlog-free operation toward hundreds of logical qubits
stages.exit: Sub-microsecond decode-feedback latency demonstrated or credibly projected at >100 logical-qubit-equivalent scale
stages.note: 446 ns at d=3 with a projection to d=21; single-CPU simulation reaches 408 logical qubits

stages.name: Feedforward timing for non-Clifford operations
stages.goal: Integrate magic-state injection and other feedforward-dependent operations into the same real-time budget as decoding
stages.exit: A real-time loop demonstrated triggering feedforward-dependent logical operations within one code cycle
stages.note: Injection protocols are being improved algorithmically, but not yet integrated into a real-time control-loop demonstration

stages.name: Formally verified, unified end-to-end guarantees at scale
stages.goal: Prove (not just measure) latency and correctness guarantees across changing codes/decoders/vendors at roadmap scale
stages.exit: A formally verified or provably-bounded guarantee published for a controller-decoder loop of roadmap-relevant size
stages.note: Existing verification work targets QEC program logic, not real-time control-loop timing

IBM.headline: Roadmap states the requirement; published work targets decoding chips, not the control-loop interface itself
IBM.summary: IBM's public work identified in this review targets decoding algorithms and FPGA decoder chips (Relay-BP, gross-code FPGA decoding) rather than the full measurement-to-correction control loop or a controller-decoder interface standard. IBM's roadmap blog states that Kookaburra (2026) and Starling (2029, 200 logical qubits/1e8 gates) require real-time qLDPC decoding integrated with control hardware, but no IBM-authored paper on end-to-end latency guarantees, backlog stability, or a controller-decoder interface specification appeared in this search.

Google.headline: Demonstrated a working real-time measurement-to-correction loop on live hardware (Willow, 2024)
Google.summary: Google's Willow processor (Nature, 2024) is the clearest public demonstration of a full real-time decode-and-correct loop: distance-5 surface-code decoding on classical hardware colocated with the chip, averaging 63 µs latency with 1.1 µs QEC cycles and no reported backlog growth. Google's RSA-cryptanalysis resource estimate assumes a 10 µs reaction-time budget for the control loop at scale, but no published Google work addresses a general controller-decoder interface standard, formal timing/correctness guarantees, or feedforward magic-state-injection timing beyond this single-code demonstration.

QuEra.headline: Roadmap cites an NVIDIA collaboration for fast decoding; no public controller co-design paper found
QuEra.summary: QuEra's Libra roadmap (2028, >256 logical qubits at 1e-6 logical error) states that fast decoding enabling real-time error correction is being developed with NVIDIA, implying eventual use of NVQLink-class infrastructure, but no QuEra-authored paper on end-to-end control-loop latency, backlog stability, or a controller-decoder interface was identified in this review. Neutral-atom transversal gates' need for correlated decoding (Cain et al., 2024) implies strict feedforward-timing requirements before the next transversal layer, but this remains unaddressed in public QuEra literature.

IonQ.headline: Decoder latency modeled as execution delay in simulation; no hardware control loop published.
IonQ.summary: IonQ's 2026 real-time decoder study models the measurement-to-correction loop in simulation: a 5-cycle error decoder and a 2-cycle outcome decoder run on 12 CPU cores, and execution is delayed whenever a needed decoding result is not ready at the next syndrome-cycle boundary. The reported delay is under 0.3% at CNOT error 1e-4 and under 12% at 5e-4, assuming 1 to 5 ms cycles. Inputs were simulated syndromes; no FPGA, controller integration or live feed-forward on IonQ hardware has been published.
IonQ.gateWhy: Bounded-latency feed-forward binds when 100+ logical qubits run 10^5 hard operations by 2028; prototype-scale runs can use a slow classical loop.

Community.headline: Most controller-decoder integration work: Riverlane/Qblox, NVIDIA NVQLink/CUDA-Q, Quantinuum, Quantum Machines, LBNL, IonQ
Community.summary: The controller-decoder co-design frontier is being built almost entirely outside IBM/Google/QuEra's headline papers. Rigetti+Riverlane (Caune et al., 2024) ran the first FPGA-integrated low-latency loop on a real superconducting QPU; Riverlane's Deltaflow/QECi now closes a full loop with Qblox at 6.9-12 µs (Surface-17/161, 2026) and published an adaptive hardware decoder in Nature Communications (2025). NVIDIA's NVQLink (2025) and CUDA-Q QEC 0.6 (2026) offer a vendor-neutral architecture already adopted by 17 hardware partners and 9 national labs, used by Quantinuum, Quantum Machines/DGX Quantum and Anyon Computing. LBNL's QubiC/RISC-Q and a UMD/LBNL open-source system (446 ns at d=3) provide open alternatives; IonQ showed single-CPU real-time decoding feasible in simulation to 408 logical qubits.

overall.headline: Multiple full hardware loops are now real-time; a shared interface standard and formal guarantees are still missing
overall.summary: Several independent groups (Google/Willow, Rigetti+Riverlane, Qblox+Riverlane, LBNL/UMD) have each closed a real-time measurement-to-correction loop at small scale, with single-digit-microsecond to sub-microsecond latencies, and NVIDIA's NVQLink is emerging as a vendor-neutral hardware-software interface with broad adoption (17 partners, 9 labs). But every demonstration is code- and vendor-specific: there is no published controller-decoder interface specification, no formal proof of end-to-end latency or Pauli-frame correctness as codes/decoders change, and no demonstrated backlog-free operation at IBM Starling/QuEra Libra roadmap scale. Feedforward timing for magic-state injection remains largely unaddressed.

gaps.gap: No standard controller-decoder interface across vendors
gaps.why_hard: Each stack (Riverlane/Qblox, NVIDIA/NVQLink, Quantinuum) defines its own timing contract and data format, so integrations are not portable
gaps.entry_point: Formalize a minimal interface (syndrome format, deadline contract, backpressure signal) and implement adapters for two existing stacks, e.g. NVQLink and QubiC/RISC-Q

gaps.gap: No formally verified end-to-end latency/correctness guarantee
gaps.why_hard: Verifying timing across a heterogeneous FPGA/GPU pipeline as decoders/codes change combines real-time-systems verification with QEC correctness proofs, a combination not yet attempted
gaps.entry_point: Apply existing QEC-program verification techniques to a fixed, small, published control loop (e.g. Caune et al.'s FPGA decoder) as a first case study

gaps.gap: Feedforward timing for magic-state injection is not integrated into real-time loops
gaps.why_hard: Injection requires fast, high-confidence classification feeding forward within the same cycle budget as decoding, and no public demonstration combines both in one real-time loop
gaps.entry_point: Extend an existing open real-time stack (QubiC/RISC-Q or NVQLink) to trigger simulated magic-state injection conditioned on decoder output within one cycle

problems.note: IBM and QuEra levels reflect published work only; both roadmaps require this loop to work at scale.
problems.name: Decoder–controller loop

doe.pullWhy: Every hard operation done by injection needs feed-forward, so even the Prototype tier's 10³ hard operations require a closed real-time loop.
doe.verifyWhy: DOE's V&V testbed explicitly evaluates classical control stack integration and execution times across the stack.

problems.title: Logical instruction sets on qLDPC memories
problems.one_liner: Design fault-tolerant, low-overhead logical measurements and gates for high-rate qLDPC code blocks, with provable fault distance, bounded space-time overhead and decodable circuits.
problems.statement: High-rate qLDPC codes such as the [[144,12,12]] gross code store many logical qubits per block at a fraction of the surface code's qubit cost, but a memory is not a computer. The problem is to equip such memories with a complete, universal logical instruction set: logical Pauli-product measurements within and between blocks (code surgery, bridges, adapters, extractors, gauging, homological measurement), automorphism, fold-transversal and transversal gates, and magic-state injection, together with decoders that handle the resulting time-varying detector graphs in real time. Each gadget must come with (i) a proof or certified computation that its fault distance is at least the memory distance d, (ii) its ancilla-qubit count and number of syndrome rounds, and (iii) circuit-level logical error rates at physical error rates near 1e-3. 'Solved' would mean constructions that work across general qLDPC code families; measure arbitrary and many simultaneous logical operators with space overhead near-linear in the measured support and constant or amortized-constant time overhead; compile algorithms with a bounded constant-factor slowdown relative to surface-code lattice surgery; and are validated on hardware with real-time decoding at module scale (tens of logical qubits).

anchors.item: Kookaburra: first module storing information in a qLDPC memory and processing it with an attached logical processing unit (LPU)
anchors.dependency: The LPU must perform in-module logical Pauli measurements on the bicycle-code memory without lowering its fault distance, using circuits decodable in real time.

anchors.item: Cockatoo: entanglement between modules using the universal adapter
anchors.dependency: Requires inter-block logical measurements (adapters or bridges) between separate code modules with bounded ancilla overhead and preserved distance.

anchors.item: Starling: 100 million gates on 200 logical qubits (Poughkeepsie)
anchors.dependency: A universal instruction set (in-module measurements, automorphisms, inter-module links, magic injection) on bicycle-code modules is the stated compilation target.

anchors.item: Milestone 4: logical gate (~10^4 physical qubits, 1e-6 logical error); undated, in progress
anchors.dependency: Indirect: Google's stated route is surface/color-code lattice surgery; qLDPC instruction sets are the main alternative for cutting footprint, not a stated dependency.

anchors.item: Libra megaquop system: 256 logical qubits (>10,000 physical) at 99.9999% logical fidelity with high-rate QEC and transversal logical operations
anchors.dependency: Computing on 256 logical qubits with roughly 40 physical qubits each requires addressable logical operations on shared high-rate code blocks.

anchors.item: Gigaquop system: >1,000 logical qubits at 1e-9 using ultra-high-rate qLDPC codes (encoding rate close to 50%)
anchors.dependency: At about two physical qubits per logical qubit, logical operations must come from surgery or transversal gadgets on shared blocks, not per-qubit patches.

criteria_why.C1: New gadget constructions (hypergraph surgery, gauging, PCPP-based surgery) and new fault-distance proofs are central; this is not replication of known engineering.
criteria_why.C2: Ancilla counts, rounds and fault distance are computable, but circuit-level logical error rates need costly Monte Carlo and exact circuit distance is expensive to certify.
criteria_why.C3: Open simulators and surgery tools allow parallel work, but no shared benchmark suite or leaderboard for gadgets on standard codes exists yet.
criteria_why.C4: Partial unification exists (homological and hypergraph surgery equivalences), but no accepted theory of optimal space-time overhead or compilation for general qLDPC codes.
criteria_why.C5: Natural ladder: single measurement, full instruction set for one code, parallel high-rate operations, hardware module, general optimality.
criteria_why.C6: Constant-time, near-linear-space fault-tolerant measurement of arbitrary logical operators on general qLDPC codes remains open; lower bounds are partial.

problems.access_note: Stim-based circuit simulation, BP-OSD or Relay-type decoders and F2 linear algebra suffice for S0-S3; hardware stages need long-range-connectivity platform partners.

metrics.name: Ancilla overhead per logical measurement
metrics.def: Extra physical qubits (and checks) added to measure a weight-w logical Pauli, as a function of w and d (qubits).
metrics.sota: Θ(w) ancillas for bridged surgery (Cross et al., IBM, 2024); linear up to polylog factors via gauging (Williamson & Yoder, Nature Physics 2026).

metrics.name: Measurement fault distance
metrics.def: Minimum number of circuit or phenomenological faults causing an undetected logical error during the gadget; must be at least the memory distance d.
metrics.sota: Distance d preserved with proofs for gauging and for PCPP-based high-rate surgery (phenomenological, d rounds; Cowtan & Ide, 2026).

metrics.name: Time overhead per logical measurement
metrics.def: Syndrome-extraction rounds per logical measurement, or amortized per measurement in a batch (QEC cycles).
metrics.sota: Amortized constant rounds via auxiliary hypergraphs and block reading (Cowtan et al., 2025); Θ(1) rounds for transversal operations (Zhou et al., Nature 2025).

metrics.name: Parallel space-time overhead vs memory
metrics.def: Space-time volume of a batch of logical measurements divided by that of an idle memory of equal duration (dimensionless).
metrics.sota: ~2x memory for up to hundreds of simultaneous random logical measurements on the gross code and 25%-rate codes (Zheng, Jiang & Xu, 2025).

metrics.name: Logical error per logical operation
metrics.def: Failure probability per logical measurement or gate under circuit-level depolarizing noise at p=1e-3 (per operation).
metrics.sota: ~1e-6 per logical measurement for a distance-10 hypergraph-product code with a full extractor at p=1e-3 (Blue et al., 2026).

metrics.name: Physical qubits per unit of logical circuit capacity
metrics.def: Physical qubits needed to run a logical circuit of given size and accuracy, relative to surface-code lattice surgery (ratio).
metrics.sota: ~10x larger logical circuits per physical qubit than surface codes (Tour de gross, IBM, 2025); 3.5x fewer qubits for [[225,16,8]] SHYPS (Photonic, 2026).
