stages.name: Simulation, decoding and metric infrastructure
stages.goal: Circuit-level simulators, decoders and shared definitions of fault distance, ancilla count and rounds for logical-operation gadgets.
stages.exit: Open tools reproduce published gadget logical error rates, and papers report the same metric set.
stages.note: Stim, BP-OSD/Relay-BP decoders and SSIP are public; Relay-BP reaches gross-code accuracy in 30-80 iterations (2025).

stages.name: Single logical measurement and gate gadgets
stages.goal: Fault-tolerantly measure one logical Pauli, or apply an automorphism or fold-transversal gate, on a qLDPC block with proven distance and near-linear ancilla overhead.
stages.exit: Construction with a proof of fault distance ≥ d and O(w polylog w) ancillas, validated by circuit-level simulation on a d ≥ 10 code.
stages.note: Bridged surgery (Θ(w)), gauging, homological measurement and adapters are proven; automorphism and fold-transversal gates are catalogued for BB codes.

stages.name: Complete instruction set for a concrete code
stages.goal: Universal instruction set (measurements, automorphisms, inter-block operations, magic injection) for one code family with end-to-end circuit-level resource estimates.
stages.exit: Published compiled instruction set with per-instruction logical error rates at p=1e-3 and algorithm-level resource estimates.
stages.note: Met in simulation for gross/two-gross BB codes (2025) and SHYPS codes (2026); not validated on hardware.

stages.name: Parallel, high-rate logical operations
stages.goal: Measure many logical operators in parallel with near-constant space-time overhead and constant-round gadgets, within and across blocks.
stages.exit: Circuit-level simulation of ≥100 simultaneous logical measurements at ≤2x memory space-time cost with preserved distance, plus a compiler using them.
stages.note: Extractors, parallel, high-rate, batched and transversal surgery proposed 2025-2026; ~2x overhead shown in simulation; decoders and compilers immature.

stages.name: Hardware logical operations on qLDPC blocks
stages.goal: Demonstrate logical measurements or gates on a qLDPC memory in hardware with real-time decoding and logical error below physical.
stages.exit: Logical Pauli measurement between qLDPC-encoded qubits at d ≥ 6, decoded in real time, with logical error below the physical-qubit baseline.
stages.note: Only small-code precursors: [[25,4,3]] logical GHZ (H2), [[16,4,4]] tesseract, [[8,3,2]] transversal gates; Google's color-code surgery is the non-qLDPC contrast.

stages.name: Optimal-overhead theory and roadmap-scale integration
stages.goal: Tight space-time overhead bounds for logical operations on general qLDPC codes, and integration into systems with 100+ logical qubits.
stages.exit: Matching upper and lower bounds for space and time, and a roadmap system (e.g., Starling, Libra) executing ≥1e6 logical operations.
stages.note: PCPP-based surgery reaches μ^(1+o(1)) size against an Ω(μ) lower bound (2026); application-scale compilations exist only as resource estimates.

IBM.headline: Leads qLDPC gadget theory; Kookaburra LPU module targeted for 2026, no hardware logic yet
IBM.summary: IBM authors or co-authors most qLDPC surgery constructions: bridged surgery with Θ(w) ancillas (2024), gauging (Nature Physics, April 2026), universal adapters, parallel surgery, extractors (2025) and constant-round auxiliary-hypergraph surgery (October 2025). 'Tour de gross' (June 2025) specifies an instruction set on gross and two-gross modules, claiming ~10x larger logical circuits per physical qubit than surface codes. Relay-BP (2025) reaches gross-code accuracy in 30-80 iterations, aimed at real-time decoding. No hardware logical operation on a qLDPC block had been published by September 2026.

Google.headline: Pursues surface/color-code lattice surgery; no public qLDPC instruction-set work
Google.summary: Google's roadmap (Milestone 4: a logical gate at ~10^4 physical qubits and 1e-6 error) relies on surface and color codes. Its color-code experiment (Nature 2025) scaled d=3 to 5 with Λ3/5 = 1.56(4), added 0.0027(3) error per transversal Clifford, and teleported logical states between distance-3 color codes by lattice surgery at 86.5-90.7% fidelity. Google researchers also co-developed SAT-based lattice-surgery synthesis (LaSsynth). No Google-authored qLDPC logical-operation paper was identified.

QuEra.headline: Theory for transversal and batched high-rate logic; hardware logic so far on small codes
QuEra.summary: QuEra-affiliated Harvard/Caltech/UChicago work proposes neutral-atom qLDPC computation: hypergraph-product codes with atom shuttling (Nature Physics 2024), parallel Pauli-product measurements with homological product codes (PRX 2025), batched high-rate gadgets claiming ~4x lower space-time cost than surface codes for Hamiltonian simulation (October 2025), and constant-round transversal fault tolerance (Nature 2025). Hardware logic so far uses small codes: 48 logical qubits in [[8,3,2]] blocks with 228 logical two-qubit gates on up to 280 atoms (Nature 2024). Libra (2028) targets 256 logical qubits with high-rate QEC.

IonQ.headline: Cat-state logical measurements and frame-tracked Cliffords designed and simulated; no hardware.
IonQ.summary: IonQ's Walking Cat architecture (April 2026) specifies logic on high-rate qLDPC memories: logical Pauli measurements through verified cat states moved next to the target qubits, a six-instruction logical instruction set, and Clifford gates handled by classical frame tracking. Components were evaluated in circuit-level simulation. The hardware experiment found (arXiv:2606.06455, at most four logical qubits per code) covers memory only; no logical gates or measurements between code blocks have been demonstrated on IonQ hardware in the sources reviewed.
IonQ.gateWhy: Even the Prototype tier (10 logical qubits, 10^3 hard operations) needs logical gates and measurements, matching IonQ's 2026 logical-qubit step.

Community.headline: Photonic, Xanadu, Oxford, Caltech/Oratomic and others drive gadgets; small hardware demos
Community.summary: Photonic Inc's SHYPS codes (Nature Communications, May 2026) implement the Clifford group transversally in O(m) rounds and match a [[784,16,7]] surface code with 3.5x fewer qubits. Xanadu introduced homological measurement; Oxford/Quantinuum released SSIP; UChicago/Caltech proposed high-rate surgery at ~2x memory cost; MIT built full extractors for hypergraph-product codes (2026); Caltech/Oratomic mitten-code processors and ~10^4-atom Shor estimates rely on Pauli-product instruction sets; Cowtan and Ide gave near-optimal PCPP-based surgery (September 2026). Hardware evidence is small: Quantinuum H2 entangled four logical qubits in a [[25,4,3]] nonlocal code beyond break-even, and Microsoft/Quantinuum ran 12-logical-qubit tesseract-code graph states.

overall.headline: Gadget theory matured rapidly in 2024-2026; parallel operations proposed; no qLDPC logic on hardware yet
overall.summary: Between 2024 and 2026 the field moved from memory-only qLDPC proposals to explicit instruction sets. Single-operator surgery with near-linear ancilla overhead and proven distance is settled in theory (S1); complete instruction sets exist in simulation for bivariate bicycle and SHYPS codes (S2); and 2025-2026 papers propose parallel, constant-round and batched operations at roughly 2x memory space-time cost (S3, partial). Bottlenecks have shifted to decoders for time-varying surgery circuits, circuit-level rather than phenomenological distance guarantees, algorithm compilation, and hardware: no logical measurement on a qLDPC block with real-time decoding has been reported, and IBM's Kookaburra (2026) is the first roadmap test.

gaps.gap: Real-time decoders for surgery and extractor circuits
gaps.why_hard: Gadgets change the detector graph over time and add high-weight, hypergraph-like checks; BP-based decoders lose accuracy on merged codes, while latency budgets are about a microsecond per round.
gaps.entry_point: Publish Stim circuits for gross-code surgery and extractor gadgets as an open benchmark, then report accuracy-latency curves for BP-OSD, Relay-type and matching-based decoders.

gaps.gap: Circuit-level fault-distance guarantees for gadgets
gaps.why_hard: Most proofs are phenomenological; hook errors from specific syndrome schedules can reduce circuit distance, and exact distance computation does not scale to large gadgets.
gaps.entry_point: Apply SAT/MaxSAT or Stim undetectable-error search to published gadgets on d ≤ 12 codes and tabulate circuit-level versus phenomenological distance.

gaps.gap: Compilers targeting parallel Pauli-product instruction sets
gaps.why_hard: Scheduling conflicts on shared ancilla systems, magic-state supply and inter-module links interact, and no standard intermediate representation or cost model spans code families.
gaps.entry_point: Build an open compiler from a benchmark circuit suite to the Tour de gross or extractor instruction set, reporting logical-cycle counts and ancilla contention.

gaps.gap: Hardware logical measurement on a qLDPC block
gaps.why_hard: Needs long-range connectivity, below-threshold errors across memory and ancilla systems, and real-time decoding at once; current demonstrations are memory-only or small codes.
gaps.entry_point: Demonstrate one bridged-surgery logical Pauli measurement on an [[18,4,4]]-class code on trapped-ion or neutral-atom hardware, first post-selected, then decoded.

gaps.gap: Time lower bounds and optimal space-time trade-offs
gaps.why_hard: Space lower bounds such as Ω(μ) exist, but limits on time overhead and their interaction with decoder speed and connectivity lack a unified theory.
gaps.entry_point: Pose the auxiliary-hypergraph cosystolic conditions as an optimization problem and search small codes for constant-round gadgets with minimal ancillas.

problems.note: Keep memory demonstrations separate from logical operations. Many fault-distance claims are phenomenological, and overhead comparisons use different baselines.
problems.name: Logic on qLDPC memories

doe.pullWhy: IBM's route to any tier runs through logic on gross-code memories, IonQ's 12-logical-qubit step needs logic on its ion-chain qLDPC codes, and Libra's 256 logical qubits need high-rate logic. Google's surface-code path does not.
doe.verifyWhy: Logical gate fidelities are on DOE's V&V list; overheads and fault distance are computable in open simulators.
doe.vv: Logical gate fidelity, fault distance and space-time overhead on high-rate codes.

problems.title: Hardware-constrained QEC code and circuit discovery
problems.one_liner: Find codes and syndrome-extraction circuits that maximize circuit-level performance per physical qubit under concrete hardware constraints such as layout, coupler length, native gates and atom movement.
problems.statement: Code tables rank quantum codes by [[n,k,d]], but a processor experiences a code through a specific syndrome-extraction circuit on a specific device. The problem is to discover, jointly, stabilizer codes, qubit layouts and syndrome-extraction schedules that are optimal under explicit hardware constraints: planar or thickness-2 coupler graphs, maximum qubit degree and coupler length, native gate sets (CZ, iSWAP), measurement and reset scheduling, and atom-movement time in zoned or shuttled arrays, plus logical-gate requirements such as transversal or automorphism gates where needed. Candidates must be evaluated at circuit level (circuit-level distance, logical error per logical qubit per round under a stated noise model, cycle time and qubit count), not by code parameters alone. 'Solved' would mean (i) reproducible search pipelines (algebraic, SAT/MILP, reinforcement learning or other ML) that return certified codes and circuits for a given constraint specification; (ii) open benchmark suites where results are comparable across groups; (iii) bounds showing how far the best constructions are from optimal for each constraint class; and (iv) at least one discovered code-circuit pair validated on hardware below threshold at a scale relevant to a roadmap module.

anchors.item: Kookaburra: first module storing information in a qLDPC memory and processing it with an attached logical processing unit
anchors.dependency: Code and syndrome circuits must fit the fabricated c-coupler routing (degree-6, two planar layers) while reaching the target circuit-level distance.

anchors.item: Starling: 100 million gates on 200 logical qubits
anchors.dependency: Module count and footprint depend on which bicycle-type codes and layouts deliver the required logical error per qubit per cycle.

anchors.item: Milestone 3: long-lived logical qubit (1e-6 logical error, ~10^3 physical qubits); undated, in progress
anchors.dependency: Hardware-aware circuits (hexagonal, iSWAP, walking) determine whether 1e-6 is reachable within the connectivity and leakage constraints of Google's processors.

anchors.item: Libra megaquop system: 256 logical qubits (>10,000 physical) with high-rate QEC and transversal logical operations
anchors.dependency: Requires high-rate codes whose syndrome extraction fits atom-movement budgets and zoned layouts while supporting transversal logical operations.

anchors.item: Gigaquop system: >1,000 logical qubits at 1e-9 using ultra-high-rate qLDPC codes (encoding rate close to 50%)
anchors.dependency: The ~50%-rate codes with projected 1e-13 memory error are announced but unpublished; discovering and certifying them under movement constraints is a prerequisite.

criteria_why.C1: Mix of new constructions (tile, directional, morphing designs) and systematic search or engineering; much progress is optimization rather than new concepts.
criteria_why.C2: kd²/n, circuit-level distance and logical error per round under fixed noise models are crisp and automatable; large-n distances and rare events remain costly.
criteria_why.C3: Code tables, open simulators and explicit constraint specifications let many groups contribute and compare results in parallel; a leaderboard is natural.
criteria_why.C4: Families (BB, 2BGA, tile, La-cross) and bounds (Baspin-Krishna, weight bounds) exist, but no framework maps hardware constraints to optimal code-circuit pairs.
criteria_why.C5: Staged from algebraic enumeration to constrained co-design, automated search, hardware validation and bounds, each with measurable exits.
criteria_why.C6: Point constructions are routine once constraints are fixed; optimality proofs and general constrained bounds remain open.

problems.access_note: Stim, a distance estimator and a GPU or small cluster for Monte Carlo suffice; hardware validation needs platform partners.

metrics.name: Encoding efficiency kd²/n
metrics.def: k·d²/n from certified [[n,k,d]] (dimensionless; rotated surface code = 1).
metrics.sota: kd²/n = 14.85 for a [[66,20,7]] bicycle code (Lu et al., 2026); 12 for the [[144,12,12]] gross code (IBM, 2024).

metrics.name: Circuit-level logical error per logical qubit per round
metrics.def: Monte Carlo logical failure rate per logical qubit per syndrome round under stated circuit noise, e.g., uniform depolarizing p=1e-3.
metrics.sota: Directional tile codes: up to 1000x lower than rotated surface-code memories at ~30 circuit qubits per logical qubit (Gu et al., 2026).

metrics.name: Connectivity cost
metrics.def: Maximum and average qubit degree, graph thickness, and number and length of long-range couplers required by the syndrome circuit.
metrics.sota: Nearest-neighbour square grid via iSWAP walks (Gu et al., 2026); average degree 4 for BB codes with Louvre-8 routing (Zhou et al., 2025).

metrics.name: Syndrome cycle time
metrics.def: Wall-clock duration of one syndrome-extraction round including atom movement, gates and measurement (seconds).
metrics.sota: ~1.28 ms per round for [[144,12,12]] with optimized long-range Rydberg gates (Poole et al., 2025).

metrics.name: Search throughput and certification cost
metrics.def: Candidate codes screened per GPU-hour, or wall time to estimate or certify distance.
metrics.sota: sQetch GPU distance estimator up to 800,000x faster than BP+OSD-based estimation; millions of candidates per hour (Bhardwaj et al., 2026).

metrics.name: Hardware logical error per cycle
metrics.def: Measured logical error per logical qubit per QEC cycle for a non-surface code on hardware (per cycle).
metrics.sota: 8.91(17)% for an [[18,4,4]] BB code on a 32-qubit long-range-coupled processor (Wang et al., 2026); IonQ reports up to 9x lower (2026).

infra.name: Stim
infra.what: Stabilizer circuit simulator with detector error models; standard for circuit-level evaluation of candidate codes.

infra.name: qLDPC library
infra.what: Builds BB, hypergraph-product, lifted-product and other codes; distance bounds via QDistRnd; Stim circuit generation.

infra.name: ldpc
infra.what: BP+OSD, BP+LSD and union-find decoders for circuit-level evaluation of candidate codes.

infra.name: Error Correction Zoo
infra.what: Open, citable catalogue of 1,149 code entries with families, parameters and references (CC BY-SA 4.0).

infra.name: MQT QECC
infra.what: MaxSAT-based decoding and synthesis of fault-tolerant state-preparation circuits for CSS codes.

stages.name: Evaluation infrastructure and code catalogues
stages.goal: Simulators, decoders, distance estimators and catalogues that evaluate any code-circuit pair under a stated noise model.
stages.exit: Open tools compute circuit-level distance and logical error for published codes and reproduce reported values within error bars.
stages.note: Stim (2021), BP-OSD/LSD decoders, the qLDPC library and the Error Correction Zoo (1,149 entries) are public.

stages.name: Algebraic enumeration under weight limits
stages.goal: Enumerate structured families (bicycle, 2BGA, multivariate, self-dual) for the best [[n,k,d]] under check-weight limits.
stages.exit: Certified tables for check weight ≤8 and n up to a few hundred, with exact or certified distances.
stages.note: 2BGA codes enumerated to n≤100 (abelian) and n≤200 (non-abelian); self-dual BB tables to ~200 qubits; [[66,20,7]] found in 2026.

stages.name: Constraint-aware code-circuit co-design
stages.goal: Design codes plus syndrome schedules for explicit constraints (thickness, degree, nearest-neighbour, iSWAP, atom movement), evaluated at circuit level.
stages.exit: For each major platform, a code-circuit pair using fewer qubits than the surface code at equal circuit-level logical error under realistic noise.
stages.note: Point designs exist for superconducting (thickness-2, morphing, directional, tile) and atom (La-cross, coprime BB, qSIEVE) hardware; noise models differ across papers.

stages.name: Automated search with circuit-level objectives
stages.goal: Search pipelines (RL, ML, SAT/MILP, GPU enumeration) that optimize circuit-level metrics under hardware constraints at hundreds of qubits.
stages.exit: Automated search returns certified codes beating hand-designed ones on a public constraint benchmark at n ≥ 100.
stages.note: RL reaches ~20 qubits (d=5) and low-weight codes; GPU search (sQetch) screens millions of candidates per hour but mainly optimizes code-level parameters.

stages.name: Hardware validation of designed codes and circuits
stages.goal: Run discovered or constraint-designed code-circuit pairs on hardware and compare measured with simulated performance.
stages.exit: A non-surface code-circuit pair with ≥4 logical qubits run over repeated rounds with logical error below the physical baseline.
stages.note: [[18,4,4]] BB on long-range couplers (8.91% per cycle); IonQ qLDPC breakeven in some instances (2026); Google validated hexagonal, walking and iSWAP circuits.

stages.name: Constrained bounds and roadmap-scale deployment
stages.goal: Tight bounds for codes under each constraint class, and deployment of discovered codes in roadmap-scale modules.
stages.exit: Bounds within a constant factor of the best constructions for a constraint class, and a roadmap module running a discovered code.
stages.note: Baspin-Krishna bounds on long-range interactions and 2026 check-weight bounds exist; no tight bounds for thickness or movement constraints.

IBM.headline: Co-designed BB codes with thickness-2 layouts; Loon c-coupler chip announced 2025
IBM.summary: IBM chose bivariate bicycle codes partly for hardware fit: the gross code's depth-7 syndrome circuit needs a degree-6 connectivity graph made of two edge-disjoint planar subgraphs, preserving 12 logical qubits in 288 physical qubits for ~1 million cycles at p=0.1% (Nature 2024). The Loon processor (announced November 2025) adds c-couplers linking distant qubits, extra routing layers and reset; IBM also reported qLDPC decoding in under 480 ns. No peer-reviewed logical-error data from Loon, and no IBM automated code-search pipeline, had been identified by September 2026.

Google.headline: Time-dynamic surface-code circuits relax hardware needs on hardware; no qLDPC search
Google.summary: Google redesigns circuits rather than codes: McEwen, Bacon and Gidney (Quantum 2023) derived surface-code circuits for hexagonal three-coupler grids, iSWAP gates and walking patches, with teraquop footprints within 25% of standard circuits. Eickbusch et al. ran all three on hardware, with Λ3/5 = 2.15(2) (hexagonal), 1.69(6) (walking) and 1.56(2) (iSWAP). Google's Stim is the community's standard evaluation tool. No Google qLDPC code-discovery work was identified; third-party planar qLDPC designs now reuse iSWAP-walk ideas.

QuEra.headline: Atom-movement-aware qLDPC designs in theory; ~50%-rate codes announced, unpublished
QuEra.summary: QuEra-affiliated work co-designs codes with atom movement: hypergraph-product codes with rearrangement (Nature Physics 2024) project surface-code crossover at several hundred physical qubits, and batched-operation work (October 2025) introduced self-dual bivariate bicycle codes at rate ~1/10 with transversal Cliffords. QuEra's June 2026 roadmap cites ultra-high-rate qLDPC families with rate close to 50% and projected 1e-13 memory error, plus a 'BB-STAR' co-design case study, but no technical paper for these codes was identified. Harvard's tricycle codes add atom-specific syndrome circuits.

IonQ.headline: Ion-chain-tailored BB5 codes designed; nine codes run on a 40-ion barium chain.
IonQ.summary: IonQ proposed BB5 qLDPC codes and syndrome-extraction circuits tuned to long trapped-ion chains; in simulation a [[48,4,7]] code reaches 5e-5 logical error per logical qubit at 1e-3 physical error. In 2026 IonQ ran nine codes, including BB5 codes up to [[30,4,5]], on one stationary chain of forty barium-133 ions with all-to-all connectivity. Logical lifetimes reached about the physical-qubit lifetime (one code marginally above), after post-selecting out detected leakage. Walking Cat adds cyclic hypergraph product codes for shuttling-based architectures.
IonQ.gateWhy: IonQ's 2026 logical-qubit milestone needs a code and syndrome circuit matched to its hardware, as its own experiments with up to 4 logical qubits per code show.

Community.headline: Many groups design platform-specific qLDPC codes; two small hardware memory demonstrations
Community.summary: Superconducting-oriented designs include tile codes (IQM/Mainz; [[512,18,19]]), Riverlane's directional codes (a quarter to a third of toric-code qubits at equal error), nearest-neighbour directional tile codes ([[323,14,15]], 2026), morphing circuits (Delft; degree 5), Louvre routing (Tsinghua; average degree 4) and Yale's oscillator routing fabric. Atom-oriented designs include La-cross (Strasbourg), coprime-BB layouts (NC State), qSIEVE (UChicago) and Rydberg layouts (Wisconsin/Infleqtion; ~1.28 ms cycles). Search spans algebraic enumeration (UC Riverside; divisor-driven search), reinforcement learning (Erlangen; UT Austin/Tsinghua) and GPU distance estimation (Caltech/Oratomic). Hardware: Zhejiang ran an [[18,4,4]] BB code on long-range couplers; IonQ reported breakeven qLDPC memories (2026).

overall.headline: Many constraint-specific designs and early automated search; circuit-level, cross-platform benchmarks still missing
overall.summary: Since IBM's thickness-2 BB design (2024), 2025-2026 papers produced code-circuit pairs for specific constraints: planar nearest-neighbour grids via iSWAP walks, degree-4 and degree-5 BB circuits, open-boundary tile codes, and atom-movement-aware layouts. Automated search has scaled from reinforcement learning on ~20 qubits to GPU pipelines screening millions of candidates per hour, but mostly optimizes code-level parameters, with circuit-level simulation applied afterwards. Hardware validation is limited to small memories ([[18,4,4]]-class codes) and Google's constrained surface-code circuits. Missing pieces are shared constraint benchmarks with fixed noise models, circuit-level objectives inside search loops, and bounds showing how close designs are to optimal.

gaps.gap: Circuit-level metrics inside the search loop
gaps.why_hard: Estimating logical error near p=1e-3 needs many Monte Carlo shots and good decoders, and circuit distance depends on the schedule, so searches usually filter on [[n,k,d]] first.
gaps.entry_point: Use circuit-level distance from undetectable-error search plus low-weight failure counts as a cheap surrogate objective, validated against full Monte Carlo on held-out codes.

gaps.gap: Shared constraint benchmarks with fixed noise models
gaps.why_hard: Papers use different noise models, decoders and baselines (toric vs rotated surface codes), so reported improvement factors are not comparable across platforms.
gaps.entry_point: Publish constraint specifications (thickness-2, nearest-neighbour square grid, zoned atoms) with fixed noise models, reference decoders and an open results table.

gaps.gap: Joint code, schedule and layout optimization
gaps.why_hard: Schedules, qubit placement and routing are coupled combinatorial problems; exhaustive search explodes, and poor schedules can erase a good code's distance.
gaps.entry_point: Formulate schedule and placement for small BB or 2BGA codes as SAT/MILP with circuit-distance constraints and compare with hand-designed depth-7 circuits.

gaps.gap: Logical-operation-aware discovery
gaps.why_hard: Codes optimized for memory may lack automorphisms, fold-transversal gates or cheap surgery, shifting cost to logical operations that searches do not score.
gaps.entry_point: Add automorphism-group size, transversal-gate availability and surgery ancilla cost as secondary objectives in existing code-search pipelines.

gaps.gap: Bounds for constrained code families
gaps.why_hard: Existing bounds cover 2D locality or counts of long-range interactions; thickness-t, degree-limited and movement-cost models lack tight bounds.
gaps.entry_point: Extend Baspin-Krishna-type arguments to thickness-2 graphs and compare the resulting bounds with the best known BB and tile codes.

problems.note: Report kd²/n alongside circuit-level metrics: high-kd²/n codes can lose distance under specific schedules. 'Best code' only makes sense per constraint class.
problems.name: Hardware-aware code discovery

doe.pullWhy: Sets how many logical qubits fit in a machine. QuEra's Libra (2028) and IonQ's 800-logical-qubit chip (2027) both depend on high-rate codes that fit their hardware; IBM and Google need better codes mainly for the 1,000-qubit tier.
doe.verifyWhy: Computable in open simulators, but results depend on hardware noise models that are not standardized.
doe.vv: kd²/n and circuit-level logical error per logical qubit per round.

problems.title: Fault-tolerant compilation and scheduling across modalities
problems.one_liner: Compiling algorithms to logical instruction sets and scheduling them across surface-code, qLDPC, and neutral-atom fault-tolerant architectures under one shared cost model.
problems.statement: Roadmap-scale fault-tolerant quantum computers will not share one hardware substrate: IBM's bicycle-code modules run Pauli-based computation, Google's superconducting devices use lattice surgery on (color-)surface codes, and QuEra's neutral atoms combine transversal gates, algorithmic fault tolerance, and physical atom movement. Each modality already has its own compiler research line -- lattice-surgery routers, qLDPC/PBC schedulers, atom-movement compilers -- but no shared framework lets one algorithm be compiled, cost-estimated, and compared across all three under the same units (logical space-time volume, wall-clock time). Solving this means defining a common logical intermediate representation and cost model, then building schedulers that jointly optimize routing, magic-state/AFT timing, and (for neutral atoms) atom-shuttling under that model, at roadmap scale (hundreds of logical qubits, ~1e8 logical gates). 'Solved' means a published, reproducible benchmark where compilers for at least two of the three modalities report comparable space-time-volume numbers for the same target circuit, backed by a scheduling theory whose per-modality specializations recover today's best known near-optimal results.

anchors.item: Bicycle-code logical instruction set ('Tour de gross'); Kookaburra 2026 -> Starling 2029 (200 logical qubits, 1e8 gates)
anchors.dependency: Needs a compiler/scheduler mapping algorithms onto bicycle-code logical instructions to reach the 1e8-gate target.

anchors.item: Milestone 4: lattice surgery / color-code transversal gates; teleportation demoed at 86.5-90.7% fidelity
anchors.dependency: Needs a lattice-surgery router/scheduler validated to preserve fidelity as circuits scale beyond single teleportation events.

anchors.item: Libra (2028): >256 logical qubits at 1e-6 error, 'High-Rate QEC' + 'Transversal Logical Operations'; Bloqade compiles to fixed-lane atom-shuttling programs
anchors.dependency: Needs a scheduler jointly optimizing transversal-gate timing, AFT syndrome rounds, and atom-shuttling moves at >256 logical qubits.

criteria_why.C1: A shared cost model/IR spanning heterogeneous FT resource models is original research, not engineering.
criteria_why.C2: Space-time volume, gate depth and wall-clock estimates are all directly computable by simulation.
criteria_why.C3: Once a shared framework exists, the compiler community already iterates fast on benchmark-driven problems like this.
criteria_why.C4: No paper found compares compiled cost numbers across surface-code, qLDPC and neutral-atom compilers today.
criteria_why.C5: Cleanly decomposes from cost-model definition to single-modality compilers to cross-modality unification.
criteria_why.C6: Underlying routing/scheduling problems are combinatorially hard; a general cross-modality theory is unsolved.

problems.access_note: Compilers are built and benchmarked via classical simulation of circuits/cost models; no quantum hardware access required.

metrics.name: Logical space-time volume
metrics.def: Physical-qubit-area x logical-cycle-time product of a compiled schedule (Litinski 2019); computed directly from the schedule.
metrics.sota: Proven near-optimal for restricted lattice-surgery instances (Beverland et al., PRX Quantum 2022); no cross-modality number published as of 2026.

metrics.name: Two-qubit gate stages / circuit depth (neutral atom)
metrics.def: Number of parallel two-qubit-gate rounds after scheduling, from the compiler's edge-coloring/graph model.
metrics.sota: Enola: 3.7x fewer gate stages and 5.9x estimated fidelity vs. OLSQ-DPQA, scaling to 10,000 qubits in 30 minutes (Tan, Lin & Cong, 2024).

metrics.name: Magic-state-factory idle/wait time
metrics.def: Fraction of scheduled logical cycles where a routed step stalls waiting on factory output, from the joint router+factory schedule.
metrics.sota: Reduced via cultivation-aware scheduling in 2025-2026 work; no roadmap-scale (1e8-gate) number yet reported.

infra.name: TQEC
infra.what: Open-source design-automation toolkit for lattice-surgery/topological FT compilation.

infra.name: liblsqecc / Lattice Surgery Compiler
infra.what: C++/Python compiler translating high-level FT programs into lattice-surgery schedules.

infra.name: Qualtran
infra.what: Google's library for expressing and resource-analyzing fault-tolerant algorithms.

infra.name: Azure Quantum Resource Estimator
infra.what: Microsoft's open resource estimator for FT algorithms across configurable architectures.

infra.name: Bloqade-lanes
infra.what: QuEra's atom-shuttle compiler translating circuits into fixed-lane atom-movement programs.

infra.name: Enola (UCLA-VAST)
infra.what: Open-source near-optimal scheduler/router/placer for neutral-atom FPQA compilation.

stages.name: Cost-model & common low-level IR foundations
stages.goal: Define space-time cost units and gate-level IRs shared across FT stacks
stages.exit: A published cost metric and an IR adopted by >=2 independent compiler papers
stages.note: Litinski's cost model and OpenQASM3/Qualtran are already a de facto shared basis.

stages.name: Near-optimal single-modality compilers
stages.goal: Provably near-optimal routing/scheduling for one FT architecture at a time
stages.exit: Polynomial-time algorithm with a proven approximation ratio, demonstrated on benchmark circuits
stages.note: Achieved separately for surface-code lattice surgery and neutral-atom FPQA scheduling.

stages.name: FT-cost-aware scheduling within a modality
stages.goal: Incorporate magic-state timing, AFT rounds and transversal-gate constraints into the scheduler
stages.exit: Compiler jointly schedules routing plus magic-state/AFT timing with reported space-time savings vs. an unscheduled baseline
stages.note: Active 2024-2026 work (zoned compilers, magic-state-aware schedulers); mostly single-modality, small-to-medium scale.

stages.name: Cross-modality shared cost model and IR
stages.goal: One IR/cost model a compiler can target to emit lattice-surgery, PBC/qLDPC, or neutral-atom schedules
stages.exit: Published comparison of >=2 modalities' compiled space-time volume for the same input algorithm under one cost accounting
stages.note: First retargetable stack (CUDA-Q Logical) announced Sept 2026; no public cross-modality benchmark numbers yet.

stages.name: Roadmap-scale end-to-end demonstration
stages.goal: Compile and schedule a real target algorithm at Starling/Libra scale (200+ logical qubits, ~1e8 gates) on at least one modality
stages.exit: Public resource estimate or hardware run matching roadmap-scale gate/qubit counts with reported wall-clock/space-time numbers
stages.note: No modality has publicly compiled and scheduled a circuit at this scale yet.

stages.name: General cross-modality scheduling theory
stages.goal: Complexity-characterized or provably near-optimal scheduling theory valid across all three modality resource models
stages.exit: A theorem/algorithm with proven guarantees shown to specialize correctly to each modality's known near-optimal results
stages.note: Not attempted in the reviewed literature.

IBM.headline: Defined bicycle-code logical ISA; no public roadmap-scale compiler demo yet.
IBM.summary: IBM's 'Tour de gross' (arXiv:2506.03094) defines a logical instruction set for gross/bicycle-code modules, targeting Kookaburra (2026) and Starling (2029, 200 logical qubits, ~1e8 gates). No IBM-published compiler paper scheduling real circuits onto this instruction set at roadmap scale was found; related community work (Extractors, PBC space-time trade-off analyses) targets the same architecture family, and IBM contributes OpenQASM 3 as a shared low-level IR.

Google.headline: Demonstrated color-code lattice-surgery teleportation (86.5-90.7% fidelity).
Google.summary: Google's Milestone 4 targets lattice surgery and transversal gates on color codes; the group has demonstrated color-code lattice-surgery teleportation at 86.5-90.7% fidelity, a small-scale hardware proof of the primitive operation compilers must schedule. Google contributes Qualtran for resource-estimating fault-tolerant algorithms, used as shared cost-accounting infrastructure. Since adding neutral atoms as a second modality (March 2026), Google itself now spans two of the three modalities this problem must unify, but no Google-authored cross-modality compiler paper was found.

QuEra.headline: Bloqade compiles to atom-shuttling programs; roadmap sets high-rate-QEC targets.
QuEra.summary: QuEra's Bloqade toolchain compiles circuits into fixed-lane atom-shuttling programs for its neutral-atom hardware, feeding the Libra target (2028, >256 logical qubits, 1e-6 error) which specifies 'High-Rate QEC' and 'Transversal Logical Operations'. The Harvard/QuEra algorithmic-fault-tolerance result (Nature, 2025) shows O(1) syndrome-extraction rounds per logical layer, a scheduling-relevant primitive, but no public paper yet compiles a full multi-gate algorithm end-to-end onto Libra-scale hardware.

IonQ.headline: Single-platform logical instruction set and compiler designed; no cross-platform cost model.
IonQ.summary: IonQ's Walking Cat paper defines six logical instructions (state preparations, in-block and inter-block measurements, frame-tracked Cliffords) and a hierarchical synthesis flow that maps programs such as Heisenberg simulation and Shor's period finding to device instructions. IonQ's September 2026 secp256k1 estimate adds a layout mapper and a scheduler for ion transport. All of this targets IonQ's own trapped-ion architecture and is estimate-only; no shared cost model across hardware platforms has been published.
IonQ.gateWhy: Programs with 10^5 hard operations on 100+ logical qubits cannot be hand-compiled; prototype-scale circuits can.

Community.headline: Most concrete FT-compilation progress is academic, one modality at a time.
Community.summary: The bulk of concrete progress is academic: UCLA's VAST lab (Tan, Cong et al.) built OLSQ-DPQA, Enola, ZAC and LaSsynth; Microsoft Quantum (Beverland et al.) proved near-optimal lattice-surgery routing; NVIDIA published the first retargetable fault-tolerant compilation stack, CUDA-Q Logical, in September 2026; Fraunhofer's Qrisp adds an explicit fault-tolerant-compilation mode to a high-level language; and open-source projects (TQEC, liblsqecc) provide shared lattice-surgery tooling. No community benchmark yet compares compiled space-time volume for the same algorithm across surface-code, qLDPC, and neutral-atom compilers.

overall.headline: Per-modality compilers are maturing fast; a shared cross-modality cost model is only now emerging.
overall.summary: Compiler research for fault-tolerant quantum computing is accelerating fastest in the neutral-atom and surface-code communities, with several near-optimal single-modality schedulers published in 2024-2025 (Enola, LaSsynth, ZAC) and magic-state/AFT-aware scheduling now an active 2025-2026 topic. IBM, Google and QuEra have each defined or demonstrated modality-specific logical operations (bicycle-code ISA, color-code lattice surgery, atom-shuttling compilation) but none has published a compiler validated at roadmap scale. The first attempt at a shared, retargetable fault-tolerant compilation stack (NVIDIA CUDA-Q Logical) appeared only in September 2026, so cross-modality unification remains at an early stage.

gaps.gap: No shared cost model spanning lattice surgery, PBC/qLDPC, and neutral-atom scheduling.
gaps.why_hard: Modalities use fundamentally different resources (2D routing area vs. connectivity graphs vs. atom-move counts), so a common unit must be defined and validated per modality first.
gaps.entry_point: Reproduce Litinski's space-time-volume metric for a PBC/qLDPC compiler and a neutral-atom compiler on one shared benchmark circuit and publish comparable numbers.

gaps.gap: Magic-state/AFT-aware scheduling is still bolted on after routing, not co-optimized with it.
gaps.why_hard: Routing and magic-state-consumption timing are solved by separate passes today; joint optimization is a coupled, combinatorially harder ILP/SAT problem.
gaps.entry_point: Extend an open SAT/ILP router (e.g. LaSsynth) to also schedule magic-state-factory output timing as a joint constraint.

gaps.gap: No open, roadmap-scale benchmark suite (200+ logical qubits, ~1e8 gates) that all three modalities' compilers can run against.
gaps.why_hard: Current compiler papers each define their own benchmark circuits at far smaller scale, so results aren't comparable and scaling behavior at roadmap size is unverified.
gaps.entry_point: Publish a benchmark repository of representative FT circuits sized to Starling/Libra targets with a common cost-reporting format, extending Qualtran/Azure-QRE output schemas.

problems.note: Most published scheduling algorithms come from academic groups. Company papers define targets and logical operations but rarely publish their schedulers.
problems.name: Cross-platform FT compilation

doe.pullWhy: A First-generation workflow must be compiled to logical instructions and magic states on every platform, and DOE's technology-neutral comparisons need one cost model.
doe.verifyWhy: Each compiled program is measurable, but no cross-platform cost model is agreed.
doe.vv: Logical space-time volume, hard and easy operation counts, wall-clock time.

problems.title: Magic-state production: cost models and qLDPC factories
problems.one_liner: Producing high-fidelity T/CCZ magic states at minimal space-time cost, with a shared cost model and factories compatible with qLDPC memories.
problems.statement: Universal fault-tolerant quantum computing needs non-Clifford resources — T or CCZ states — that Clifford-only error correction cannot produce, and every architecture must manufacture them at very high fidelity and low space-time cost. The open problem is finding, for a chosen code family (surface code or high-rate qLDPC), the cheapest way to produce these states — via distillation, cultivation, code switching, transversal or fold-transversal non-Clifford gates, or direct injection — and to compare protocols on a common cost metric such as qubit-rounds per T/CCZ state at a target output infidelity. 'Solved' means a validated, protocol-agnostic cost model with experimental confirmation across platforms, plus magic-state factories that live natively inside qLDPC memory blocks (not bolted onto a separate surface-code patch) so that IBM's gross-code Starling-class machines, Google's superconducting devices, and QuEra's neutral-atom arrays can each supply the roughly 10^7-10^8 magic states a useful fault-tolerant algorithm requires without the factory dominating the device's qubit budget.

anchors.item: Magic state cultivation: T-states grown directly, then switched into a surface code
anchors.dependency: Provides the low-overhead non-Clifford supply dense qLDPC-era algorithms will need

anchors.item: 2025 hardware demonstration of magic-state cultivation with code switching
anchors.dependency: Validates cultivation on real superconducting qubits: 40x error reduction, fidelity 0.9999(1), 8% retained

anchors.item: Color-code magic-state injection in simulation: over 99% fidelity, ~75% kept
anchors.dependency: Feeds the cultivation pipeline's first stage before switching to the surface code

anchors.item: Starling (2029): fault-tolerant machine running 10^8-gate circuits on gross-code modules
anchors.dependency: Needs magic-state factories that fit inside gross-code (qLDPC) modules at that gate volume

criteria_why.C1: New protocols (cultivation, zero-level, constant-overhead distillation, qLDPC codes) need genuine theoretical advances, not routine engineering.
criteria_why.C2: Qubit-rounds per T/CCZ state at fixed output infidelity is directly computable by circuit-level simulation.
criteria_why.C3: Once a cost model or code exists, many independent groups iterate on it, as shown by 2024-2026 follow-on papers.
criteria_why.C4: Litinski's cost model is a partial standard, but cultivation, distillation and injection are still compared inconsistently.
criteria_why.C5: Splits cleanly into cost-model definition, protocol simulation, hardware validation, qLDPC-native construction, and at-scale integration.
criteria_why.C6: Building good-distance qLDPC codes with transversal non-Clifford gates is an open, hard coding-theory construction problem.

problems.access_note: Small demos run on Quantinuum/IBM cloud hardware; gross-code-scale qLDPC factories exist only in simulation.

metrics.name: Qubit-rounds per T-state at target logical infidelity
metrics.def: Physical qubits x code cycles consumed per output T-state at a stated logical infidelity (Litinski's cost metric).
metrics.sota: Cultivation reaches 2e-9 logical error at 1e-3 physical noise using roughly 10x fewer qubit-rounds than distillation (Gidney, Shutty & Jones, Google, 2024).

metrics.name: Hardware logical non-Clifford gate infidelity
metrics.def: Measured infidelity of an encoded T/CCZ/CH logical gate on real qubits, with reported post-selection/discard rate.
metrics.sota: CH-gate logical infidelity <=2.3e-4 (vs 1e-3 unencoded) at 14.8% discard, magic-state infidelity 7e-5, on a 20-qubit trapped-ion processor (Dasu et al., Quantinuum, 2025).

metrics.name: Distillation overhead exponent (gamma)
metrics.def: Asymptotic scaling of protocol overhead with target output error epsilon (overhead ~ epsilon^-gamma); gamma=0 is optimal constant overhead.
metrics.sota: First constant-overhead (gamma=0) protocol, down from 0.678, via 2^10-dimensional algebraic-geometry-code qudits (Wills, Hsieh & Yamasaki, 2024/25).

metrics.name: qLDPC code distance under transversal non-Clifford support
metrics.def: Achievable code distance D(N) for an N-qubit qLDPC family that still supports a transversal or single-shot non-Clifford gate.
metrics.sota: Distance Omega(N^2/3), beating the prior sqrt(N) barrier, enabling Theta(N^1/3) simultaneous logical CCZ states without distillation (Zhu, IBM, 2025).

infra.name: Stim
infra.what: Open-source fast stabilizer circuit simulator used to compute logical error rates for magic-state circuits.

infra.name: Error Correction Zoo
infra.what: Open catalog of QEC codes, including transversal and magic-state-relevant code families.

stages.name: Cost-model baseline
stages.goal: Define a protocol-agnostic space-time cost metric for non-Clifford resource production.
stages.exit: A published qubit-rounds-per-T-state metric adopted across distillation-protocol papers.
stages.note: Litinski's 2019 cost model remains the reference metric used across the field.

stages.name: Single-protocol theoretical improvements
stages.goal: Cut simulated qubit-rounds or error per magic state via a new protocol.
stages.exit: A published protocol showing >=10x reduction in qubit-rounds at matched output infidelity.
stages.note: Cultivation, zero-level and constant-overhead distillation each report order-of-magnitude or asymptotic gains.

stages.name: Small-scale hardware validation
stages.goal: Demonstrate a logical non-Clifford gate or magic state on real qubits beating the physical baseline.
stages.exit: Reported logical infidelity below the platform's physical two-qubit gate error, on hardware.
stages.note: Quantinuum reached break-even logical CH-gate fidelity in 2025; Google reported a matching 2025 cultivation hardware result.

stages.name: qLDPC-native factories and code constructions
stages.goal: Build magic-state factories and codes that live inside high-rate qLDPC memory blocks.
stages.exit: A simulated qLDPC-block factory with space-time cost competitive with surface-code factories.
stages.note: Tricycle, bicycle-architecture and in-situ injection factories exist in simulation; none yet run on real qLDPC hardware.

stages.name: Common cross-platform cost benchmark
stages.goal: Compare cultivation, distillation and injection protocols on identical noise models and metrics.
stages.exit: A published benchmark reporting qubit-rounds-per-T for >=3 protocols on >=2 hardware platforms.
stages.note: No independent benchmark suite yet unifies these protocols' cost numbers across platforms.

stages.name: At-scale gross-code integration
stages.goal: Run magic-state factories at the rate roadmap-scale algorithms need inside modular qLDPC machines.
stages.exit: A vendor sustains magic-state production meeting a 10^8-gate algorithm's budget on a qLDPC-based prototype.
stages.note: IBM states Starling (2029) needs this; no public factory numbers yet exist for gross-code hardware.

IBM.headline: Strong qLDPC code theory; no public hardware factory yet
IBM.summary: IBM researcher Guanyu Zhu published two related qLDPC constructions with transversal non-Clifford gates: an earlier one using higher-form symmetries and triple intersection numbers for parallelizable Clifford and non-Clifford logical gates on homological qLDPC codes (2023), and a later one breaking the sqrt(N) distance barrier while keeping transversal CCZ gates, enabling single-shot preparation of many independent magic states (2025). IBM's roadmap states Starling (2029) needs magic-state factories compatible with gross-code (bivariate bicycle) modules for 100-million-gate circuits, but public demonstrations of an actual factory on IBM's own hardware were not found; most bicycle-code-native factory designs come from outside academic groups.

Google.headline: Cultivation theory (2024) and first hardware demonstration (2025)
Google.summary: Google introduced magic state cultivation, which in simulation reaches about 2e-9 T-state error at 1e-3 physical noise for roughly the cost of a lattice-surgery CNOT (Gidney, Shutty & Jones, 2024). On Willow it injected magic states into the color code at over 99% fidelity while keeping about 75% of runs, and in 2025 it demonstrated cultivation with code switching into a surface code: error fell 40-fold to a state fidelity of 0.9999(1), keeping 8% of attempts.

QuEra.headline: Theoretical qLDPC factories, plus a first hardware distillation demo
QuEra.summary: A Harvard-based team including QuEra co-founder Mikhail Lukin proposed 'magic tricycle' codes, generalizing bicycle codes to three homological dimensions to generate logical CCZ states with constant-depth circuits; 50-100-qubit blocks reach logical error at or below 6e-10 with modest post-selection above a 0.5% circuit-noise threshold (Menon et al., 2025). The same Harvard/QuEra collaboration also reported the first hardware demonstration of logical-level magic-state distillation, on a neutral-atom processor using d=3 and d=5 color codes, showing improved output-state fidelity over the input logical magic states (Rodriguez et al., Nature 645, 2025).

IonQ.headline: Two H-type magic-state factory designs for qLDPC codes; simulation only.
IonQ.summary: IonQ's Walking Cat architecture produces non-Clifford resource states directly inside qLDPC codes instead of using surface-code distillation or cultivation. One 'MEK' factory distills two logical H-type states from ten physical ones using a custom [[n,6,d]] code; a 'CH2' factory uses a [[54,2,10]] code with a strongly transversal H gate and verifies states by measurement. A 110-logical-qubit configuration is estimated at about one million T gates per day. Results are simulation-based; no magic-state production on hardware is published.
IonQ.gateWhy: IonQ's 2027-2028 steps are the first needing non-Clifford throughput at scale (10^5 hard operations); 10^3 operations at prototype scale could use small-scale injection.

Community.headline: Very active: cost-model refinements, qLDPC constructions, cheaper protocols
Community.summary: The field's shared cost metric (Litinski, 2019) underlies most later work. Beyond IBM, Google and QuEra, contributions come from Quantinuum (break-even non-Clifford gate, 2025), Osaka's Fujii group (zero-level distillation, 2024), Yamasaki-Hsieh-Wills (constant-overhead distillation, 2024/25, Nature Physics), Golowich-Guruswami (qLDPC transversal codes, STOC 2025), and Yale's Ding group, which designed both bicycle-code-native distillation factories and an in-situ multi-state injection scheme (2025-26), plus a Hebrew University/Sydney team adapting cultivation to erasure-qubit surface codes.

overall.headline: Fast theoretical progress; qLDPC-native factories still unproven on hardware
overall.summary: Since 2024, magic-state production has moved from costly distillation toward cultivation and constant-overhead protocols, with Google validating cultivation in both simulation and (2025) real hardware. qLDPC coding theory has produced new transversal non-Clifford constructions (Golowich-Guruswami; Zhu) and dedicated qLDPC-native factories (tricycles, bicycle-architecture distillation, in-situ injection), mostly from academic and QuEra/Harvard-affiliated groups rather than IBM's or QuEra's own labs. No published benchmark yet compares cultivation, distillation and injection on common qubit-rounds-per-T terms, and no qLDPC-native factory has run on real hardware at the scale IBM's Starling roadmap requires.

gaps.gap: No unified cross-platform magic-state cost benchmark
gaps.why_hard: Reimplementing cultivation, distillation and injection under one noise model and metric requires substantial simulation engineering across groups.
gaps.entry_point: Build an open Stim-based suite reporting qubit-rounds-per-T at fixed infidelity for several published protocols side by side.

gaps.gap: qLDPC-native factories unverified on real hardware
gaps.why_hard: Tricycle and bicycle-code factories exist only in simulation and need long-range qubit connectivity current chips do not yet provide at scale.
gaps.entry_point: Simulate a small tricycle- or bicycle-code factory on an existing emulator, then request time on a qLDPC-capable testbed to test one module.

gaps.gap: General good-distance qLDPC codes with transversal non-Clifford gates
gaps.why_hard: Balancing high distance, high encoding rate and transversal non-Clifford support at once is an open coding-theory construction problem.
gaps.entry_point: Extend the Golowich-Guruswami or Zhu constructions to explicit, finite-length codes with a practical decoder.

problems.note: Post-selection matters: Google's hardware cultivation keeps 8% of attempts, so compare protocols on accepted-rate-adjusted cost, not fidelity alone.
problems.name: Magic-state factories

doe.pullWhy: DOE counts hard operations: 10³ for a Prototype and 10⁵ for First generation. Every roadmap needs a magic-state supply to get there.
doe.verifyWhy: This is the DOE tier metric itself.
doe.vv: Hard operations completed reliably; T-state fidelity, acceptance and qubit-rounds per state.

problems.title: QEC-native noise learning and syndrome-based digital twins
problems.one_liner: Learn correlated, drifting noise directly from syndrome data to calibrate decoders and build certified digital twins forecasting logical error rates.
problems.statement: Fault-tolerant QEC decoders assume a known noise process, but real devices show correlated, non-stationary, drifting noise no static model captures. The problem is to learn detector error models and richer noise descriptions directly from the syndrome and detection-event statistics that QEC circuits already produce, without added characterization circuits, then use them to calibrate decoders and forecast logical error rates on circuits, codes, or scales never directly measured. This requires an identifiability analysis of which noise parameters syndrome statistics can and cannot distinguish, uncertainty quantification on the learned model, and certification of predictions when the device drifts away from the training distribution. 'Solved' means a validated pipeline, noise inference plus decoder calibration plus a digital-twin predictor with calibrated error bars, that keeps logical-error-rate forecasts accurate as devices scale from hundreds to millions of physical qubits and drift over hours to months of operation.

anchors.item: Reinforcement learning tunes 1,000+ analog control parameters online from syndrome data during QEC (d=7 error 7.72e-4/cycle, up to 3.5x better drift stability)
anchors.dependency: Needs syndrome-based drift/noise inference to know what to retune and to certify gains persist

anchors.item: Willow: Lambda=2.14, distance-7 error 0.143%/cycle; repetition codes reach ~1e-10/cycle at d=29 but correlated bursts occur roughly hourly
anchors.dependency: Burst-aware forecasting needs a noise model capturing rare correlated events, not just a steady-state detector error model

anchors.item: Kookaburra/Starling qLDPC architectures need noise models for long-range c-coupler syndrome-extraction circuits
anchors.dependency: Long-range qLDPC couplers create correlated-error pathways that syndrome-based noise-learning tools validated on local surface codes have not covered

criteria_why.C1: Identifiability, uncertainty quantification, and certification under drift are open research questions, not engineering tasks
criteria_why.C2: Logical error rate, DEM likelihood, and decoder-calibration gain are all directly computable from syndrome data
criteria_why.C3: Public syndrome datasets and open decoders (Stim, PyMatching) let the community iterate without owning hardware
criteria_why.C4: Partial frameworks exist (sparse Pauli-Lindblad, DEMs) but no certified digital-twin framework spans drift and distribution shift
criteria_why.C5: Splits cleanly from identifiability theory to scalable learning to online adaptation to certified forecasting
criteria_why.C6: General identifiability and certification proofs under time-varying, correlated noise are mathematically hard

problems.access_note: Google and IBM publish syndrome/detection-event datasets (Zenodo) and open decoders, enabling noise-learning research without owning hardware.

metrics.name: Detector error model fit quality
metrics.def: Log-likelihood or KL divergence between a learned DEM's predicted detection-event correlations and held-out syndrome data
metrics.sota: Sparse Pauli-Lindblad models learned and validated on 100+-qubit IBM hardware for probabilistic error cancellation (van den Berg et al., Nature Physics 2023)

metrics.name: Logical error rate prediction accuracy
metrics.def: Difference between a decoder/digital-twin's predicted logical error rate and the measured rate at a held-out code distance or circuit
metrics.sota: AlphaQubit trained on 25 rounds generalizes to 100,000 rounds and beats correlated matching by 1.25x at distance 11 in simulation (Google DeepMind, Nature 2024)

metrics.name: Decoder calibration gain
metrics.def: Change in logical error rate when decoder edge-weight priors are learned/optimized from experimental data versus left at uniform defaults
metrics.sota: Optimized decoder priors measurably improve logical error rate over uniform priors on Google superconducting hardware (Sivak et al., PRL 2024)

metrics.name: Drift-stability retention
metrics.def: Logical error rate stability over hours of continuous operation under periodic recalibration from live syndrome data
metrics.sota: RL controller sustains d=7 error at 7.72e-4/cycle with up to 3.5x better drift stability than fixed calibration (Google, Nature 2026)

infra.name: Stim
infra.what: Fast stabilizer-circuit simulator producing detector error models and syndrome data for decoder and noise-learning research

infra.name: Google QEC public datasets
infra.what: Released Sycamore/Willow syndrome and detection-event data used by community noise-learning and decoder studies

infra.name: PyMatching
infra.what: Open-source minimum-weight perfect matching decoder used as the baseline for calibrated-prior experiments

infra.name: Real-time quantum trajectory simulator
infra.what: USC/AWS open-system Monte Carlo simulator scaling coherent/correlated-noise digital-twin modeling to distance-7 surface codes

stages.name: Infrastructure: simulators, public syndrome datasets, baseline DEMs
stages.goal: Make syndrome data, decoders, and detector error models publicly available and standardized
stages.exit: Public dataset plus open decoder pipeline usable without owning hardware
stages.note: Stim, PyMatching, and Google's public syndrome datasets are mature and widely used

stages.name: Single-channel Pauli noise identifiability and learning from syndromes
stages.goal: Prove which noise parameters syndrome statistics identify and learn them efficiently
stages.exit: Demonstrated Pauli noise model recovery from syndrome-only data on real hardware
stages.note: Identifiability proofs and efficient learning shown on small-to-medium devices

stages.name: Scalable correlated/sparse noise-model and decoding-graph learning at hardware scale
stages.goal: Extend noise learning to sparse correlated and coherent-error models at 100+ qubits
stages.exit: Learned noise/decoding-graph model validated against held-out hardware data at 100+ qubits
stages.note: Sparse Pauli-Lindblad and decoding-graph estimation scale to 100+ qubits; general coherent/correlated noise remains costly

stages.name: Noise-aware, adaptive, and ML decoders exploiting learned noise online
stages.goal: Use learned/online noise information to actively improve decoding and control in real time
stages.exit: On-hardware demonstration of improved logical error rate or drift stability from online noise-aware adaptation
stages.note: AlphaQubit and Google's RL controller show gains at Sycamore/Willow scale; untested at qLDPC or million-qubit scale

stages.name: Predictive digital twins with uncertainty quantification for unseen circuits/codes/scales
stages.goal: Forecast logical error rates on new codes/scales with calibrated, certified uncertainty
stages.exit: Published forecast with calibrated error bars validated against held-out hardware at a new scale
stages.note: No published certified logical-error-rate forecasting pipeline with calibrated uncertainty was found

stages.name: Certified theory integrated with roadmap-scale long-range qLDPC architectures
stages.goal: Extend certified noise learning and forecasting to long-range-coupler qLDPC codes at roadmap scale
stages.exit: Published noise model and certified forecast for a long-range c-coupler qLDPC syndrome-extraction circuit
stages.note: IBM's long-range c-coupler qLDPC circuits currently lack any published noise model

IBM.headline: Sparse Pauli-Lindblad learning at 100+ qubits, for mitigation rather than syndromes
IBM.summary: IBM's sparse Pauli-Lindblad models (van den Berg et al., Nature Physics 2023; Quantum 2024) learn correlated Pauli noise from cycle-benchmarking-style data on 100+-qubit devices, primarily to support probabilistic error cancellation rather than decoder calibration. No public noise model has yet been demonstrated for Kookaburra/Starling's long-range c-coupler qLDPC syndrome-extraction circuits, which the roadmap will require.

Google.headline: On-hardware decoder calibration, ML decoding, and RL-based drift control from syndromes
Google.summary: Google has shown the most complete syndrome-based noise-learning-to-action pipeline: optimized decoder priors (Sivak et al., PRL 2024), the AlphaQubit ML decoder generalizing from 25 to 100,000 rounds (Nature 2024), and a July 2026 Nature paper using reinforcement learning on syndrome data to tune 1,000+ control parameters, reaching d=7 error 7.72e-4/cycle with up to 3.5x better drift stability.

QuEra.headline: No public syndrome-based noise-learning or digital-twin work found
QuEra.summary: Searches for QuEra-specific detector-error-model learning, decoder calibration, or digital-twin work targeting syndrome/detection-event data returned nothing; QuEra's public research effort concentrates on atom loss and erasure handling (see P10) rather than syndrome-based noise learning or forecasting.

IonQ.headline: No public IonQ work on learning correlated or drifting noise from syndromes.
IonQ.summary: No IonQ-authored work was found on learning correlated or drifting noise from syndrome statistics for decoder calibration or digital twins. The closest item is the 2026 breakeven experiment, where decoder noise parameters came from gate-set tomography and randomized benchmarking and were then hand-tuned by repeatedly decoding the hardware data to minimize summed logical error.
IonQ.gateWhy: No IonQ roadmap item references learned noise models or digital twins.

Community.headline: Broad academic base in identifiability theory, decoding-graph estimation, and noise-aware decoding
Community.summary: University of Sydney groups (Harper, Flammia, Doherty, Hockings) built efficient and scalable noise-characterization protocols including ACES; a German group (Wagner et al.) proved syndrome-only Pauli-channel identifiability; TU Delft's Spitz proposed early adaptive decoder weights for drifting noise. Multiple 2025 preprints extend decoding-graph estimation, coherent-error DEMs, and noise-aware decoding, though a certified digital-twin forecasting framework has not yet appeared.

overall.headline: ML decoders and RL control now learn from syndromes on hardware; certified digital twins are unbuilt
overall.summary: 2024-2026 brought fast, concrete progress: IBM's sparse Pauli-Lindblad models scale noise learning to 100+ qubits, Google's AlphaQubit and decoder-prior optimization improve decoding using learned/experimental data, and Google's July 2026 Nature paper closes the loop with online RL control from syndromes. What is still missing is a certified digital twin: a model with calibrated uncertainty that forecasts logical error rates on genuinely new codes, scales, or drift conditions, and any public treatment of noise for long-range qLDPC couplers.

gaps.gap: No certified logical-error-rate forecasting with calibrated uncertainty for unseen circuits/codes
gaps.why_hard: Requires proving which learned noise parameters generalize beyond the training distribution under real hardware drift, not just fitting historical data
gaps.entry_point: Benchmark existing DEM-learning methods on held-out code distances using Google's public syndrome datasets and report calibration error

gaps.gap: No published noise model for IBM's long-range c-coupler qLDPC syndrome-extraction circuits
gaps.why_hard: qLDPC checks couple distant qubits, creating correlated-error pathways that local surface-code DEM tools were not designed to capture
gaps.entry_point: Extend ACES or sparse Pauli-Lindblad estimators to a simulated long-range-coupler qLDPC circuit and test whether local-noise assumptions still hold

gaps.gap: Identifiability limits of syndrome-only learning are uncharacterized for correlated, non-Markovian noise
gaps.why_hard: Many distinct time-correlated noise processes can produce statistically indistinguishable syndrome distributions, proven so far only for simple Pauli models
gaps.entry_point: Extend Wagner et al.'s identifiability analysis to time-correlated and leakage-coupled noise channels in simulation

problems.note: Online learning from syndromes on hardware (Google, 2026) is vendor-reported and not yet reproduced elsewhere; public syndrome datasets from other vendors are scarce.
problems.name: Noise learning from syndromes

doe.pullWhy: 10⁵ reliable hard operations need logical error near 10⁻⁶ per operation, which depends on decoders tuned to correlated, drifting noise. The RFA asks each applicant for its logical noise floor.
doe.verifyWhy: Computable on held-out syndrome data, but public datasets are scarce and no protocol is shared.
doe.vv: Error in predicting logical error rates from syndrome-learned models.

problems.title: Non-Pauli errors in QEC: leakage, loss, erasure, bursts
problems.one_liner: Detect, convert, and decode around leakage, atom loss, erasure, and correlated bursts across platforms, and unify them in one framework.
problems.statement: Real qubits fail in ways standard Pauli-noise QEC theory does not model: transmons leak into non-computational states, neutral atoms are lost from traps, and both can be deliberately converted into heralded 'erasure' errors that are easier to correct than unlocated Pauli errors. Superconducting arrays also suffer correlated bursts from cosmic rays and other high-energy events that violate the independent-error assumptions used to prove thresholds. Each failure mode currently has its own detection scheme, decoder modification, and threshold analysis, built platform by platform (transmon leakage removal, atom reloading, dual-rail erasure qubits), with no shared theory connecting them. 'Solved' means detection and conversion methods, loss- and leakage-aware decoders and scheduling, and threshold proofs that work at the qubit counts roadmaps require, compose correctly when several non-Pauli error types occur together, and sit inside one unifying noise-and-decoding framework general enough to cover transmons, neutral atoms, and dual-rail or bosonic encodings rather than a separate ad hoc treatment per hardware platform.

anchors.item: Libra (2028) roadmap lists 'Qubit Loss Detection & Active Reloading' as a required capability
anchors.dependency: Needs loss-aware decoders and scheduling proven at scale, not just reloading hardware

anchors.item: Harvard/QuEra reported continuous reloading of a 3,000-atom array for over two hours
anchors.dependency: Continuous operation must be paired with loss-aware QEC decoding to translate into logical uptime

anchors.item: Correlated phase-error bursts from high-energy impacts still occur about once every 71 s on average in a gap-engineered transmon array
anchors.dependency: Needs burst detection plus a decoder or scheduling response, since gap engineering alone does not eliminate bursts

anchors.item: Kookaburra/Starling long-range c-coupler qLDPC circuits need noise models covering non-local error pathways
anchors.dependency: No published leakage or erasure treatment yet exists for long-range-coupler qLDPC syndrome extraction

criteria_why.C1: A unifying theory of leakage, loss, erasure, and correlated bursts needs original research, not engineering
criteria_why.C2: Leakage population, loss/erasure threshold, and logical error rate are all directly computable feedback metrics
criteria_why.C3: Open simulators supporting erasure and loss channels let the community iterate on decoders without lab hardware
criteria_why.C4: No unified framework exists today; transmon leakage, atom loss, dual-rail erasure, and bursts are treated separately
criteria_why.C5: Decomposes into detection/conversion, loss-aware decoding, at-scale thresholds, and a unifying framework
criteria_why.C6: General threshold theorems for correlated, non-Markovian, mixed-error-type noise are non-trivial though partial results exist

problems.access_note: Decoder and scheduling theory can be simulated with open erasure/loss channel models; validating thresholds needs neutral-atom or superconducting lab hardware.

metrics.name: Leakage population per qubit
metrics.def: Fraction of qubit population outside the computational {0,1} subspace, measured via leakage-sensitive readout, averaged per QEC cycle
metrics.sota: Data Qubit Leakage Removal reduces average leakage population to about 0.1% from nearly 1% (Google, Nature Physics 2023)

metrics.name: Atom-loss/erasure threshold
metrics.def: Maximum loss or erasure rate below which logical error rate still decreases with code distance, from decoder simulation
metrics.sota: Adaptive loss-aware decoder tolerates about 2.6% atom loss per cycle with no other noise sources (Perrin et al., 2024/2025)

metrics.name: Continuous operation uptime
metrics.def: Duration and atom count over which a neutral-atom array sustains array occupation via continuous reloading
metrics.sota: 3,000-atom array held continuously for over two hours (Chiu et al., Nature 2025)

metrics.name: False-alarm rate in leakage detection
metrics.def: Fraction of leakage-triggered corrective circuits invoked when no leakage actually occurred, versus a baseline heuristic
metrics.sota: Gladiator framework cuts false alarms by up to 3x versus prior heuristics across surface, color, and qLDPC codes (Mude & Tannu, 2025)

stages.name: Infrastructure: leakage/erasure/loss channel models and simulators
stages.goal: Provide open simulators and channel models for leakage, loss, and erasure
stages.exit: Open simulator supports leakage/erasure/loss channels usable without lab hardware
stages.note: Stim and Bloqade support erasure/loss channel simulation for decoder research

stages.name: Detection and conversion demonstrations
stages.goal: Demonstrate leakage removal, atom-loss heralding, and dual-rail erasure conversion on hardware
stages.exit: Hardware demonstration converting a leakage/loss event into a heralded, locatable error
stages.note: Multiple platforms (transmon, neutral atom, dual-rail cavity) have hardware demonstrations

stages.name: Loss- and leakage-aware decoders and scheduling theory
stages.goal: Build decoders and scheduling that exploit located loss/leakage/erasure information
stages.exit: Simulated or hardware decoder shows order-of-magnitude logical error reduction using location information
stages.note: Adaptive decoders and leakage-speculation frameworks show large simulated gains; not yet unified across error types

stages.name: At-scale demonstrations combining continuous operation with loss-aware QEC
stages.goal: Scale loss/leakage-aware QEC to thousands of qubits with sustained continuous operation
stages.exit: Thousand-plus-qubit demonstration combining continuous reloading or leakage removal with QEC-relevant decoding
stages.note: 3,000-atom continuous reloading and loss-exploiting algorithms demonstrated; not yet combined with full logical QEC at that scale

stages.name: Correlated bursts (cosmic-ray/TLS) detection and mitigation
stages.goal: Detect and mitigate correlated high-energy-event bursts with a decoder-level response
stages.exit: Demonstrated decoder or scheduling response that suppresses burst-driven logical error spikes
stages.note: Gap engineering reduces but does not eliminate bursts; no integrated decoder-level response was found

stages.name: Unified cross-platform theory and roadmap-scale integration
stages.goal: Unify leakage, loss, erasure, and bursts under one noise-and-threshold framework at roadmap scale
stages.exit: Published general threshold theorem or framework covering multiple non-Pauli error types across platforms
stages.note: No unifying framework across transmon leakage, atom loss, dual-rail erasure, and bursts was found

IBM.headline: No IBM leakage-, loss- or erasure-aware QEC paper identified
IBM.summary: No IBM-authored paper on leakage-, loss- or erasure-aware QEC was identified in this review. IBM's roadmap relies on long-range c-coupler syndrome circuits (Loon, 2025; Kookaburra, 2026) whose leakage and correlated-error behavior has not been published. The level reflects public evidence only.

Google.headline: Leads leakage removal and correlated-burst characterization on superconducting hardware
Google.summary: Google's Data Qubit Leakage Removal (Miao, McEwen et al., Nature Physics 2023) cut average leakage population from about 1% to 0.1% on a transmon grid. A follow-up gap-engineered device study found correlated phase-error bursts from cosmic-ray-like high-energy impacts still occur about once every 71 s on average in a gap-engineered array, showing detection alone does not solve the burst problem.

QuEra.headline: Leads neutral-atom loss detection, continuous reloading, and loss-aware decoding at thousand-qubit scale
QuEra.summary: Harvard/QuEra demonstrated continuous reloading of a coherent 3,000-atom array for over two hours (Chiu et al., Nature 2025), and the same ecosystem produced algorithms that actively leverage known atom-loss locations (MIT/Harvard Center for Ultracold Atoms, 2025) rather than merely tolerating loss. QuEra's 2028 Libra roadmap names active reloading and loss detection as required capabilities.

IonQ.headline: Leakage detection with post-selection run on hardware; chain loss and leakage handling simulated.
IonQ.summary: In IonQ's 2026 qLDPC experiment on a 40-ion barium chain, detected leakage was handled by post-selection (18.8% to 74.8% of shots rejected depending on code), with simulations comparing erasure conversion against discarding. A November 2025 paper, co-authored with a University of Maryland researcher, uses beacon qubits to detect whole-chain loss and decodes it as erasures in simulation; a [[72,12,6]] BB code stays within 3x of the no-loss logical error at p=1e-3 for loss rate p^1.7. Walking Cat adds simulated leakage reset and loss reservoirs.
IonQ.gateWhy: IonQ's own 2026 qLDPC experiment already discarded 19%-75% of shots on detected leakage, so leakage handling is needed at prototype scale.

Community.headline: Broad industry-and-academic ecosystem builds dual-rail/erasure hardware and loss/leakage-aware decoding theory
Community.summary: AWS Center for Quantum Computing demonstrated a long-coherence dual-rail erasure qubit with tunable transmons (Levine et al., PRX 2024), and Quantum Circuits Inc. demonstrated erasure-detected logical measurement in a dual-rail superconducting cavity qubit. Princeton's Thompson lab proposed and demonstrated neutral-atom erasure conversion; a Wisconsin-Madison group (Mude & Tannu, 2025) built a leakage-speculation decoder framework; French academic groups advanced loss-aware surface-code decoding (Perrin et al.) and correlated-loss exploitation (2026 preprint).

overall.headline: Per-platform leakage/loss/erasure handling is maturing fast; a unifying framework is missing
overall.summary: 2023-2026 produced strong platform-specific progress: leakage removal on transmons, mid-circuit erasure conversion and continuous reloading on neutral atoms, and dual-rail erasure qubits on superconducting cavities, alongside decoders that exploit location information for order-of-magnitude logical error gains. What has not appeared is a single framework proving thresholds when leakage, loss, erasure, and correlated bursts interact, or any published treatment of these effects for IBM's long-range qLDPC couplers.

gaps.gap: No single theory unifies leakage, atom loss, erasure, and correlated bursts across platforms
gaps.why_hard: Each error type has a different physical origin and detection method, and general threshold proofs need a common noise-channel abstraction
gaps.entry_point: Formalize a shared 'located-or-heralded error' channel covering post-removal leakage, detected atom loss, and erasure qubits, then re-derive existing threshold results inside it

gaps.gap: Correlated high-energy-event bursts persist after gap engineering with no decoder-level response demonstrated
gaps.why_hard: Bursts are rare, spatially correlated, and short-lived, so standard per-round independent-error decoders are not built to react to them
gaps.entry_point: Use published cosmic-ray burst statistics to build and simulate a burst-triggered decoding-graph reweighting scheme, tested on Willow-scale syndrome data

gaps.gap: IBM's long-range qLDPC c-coupler circuits have no published leakage or erasure treatment
gaps.why_hard: Non-local couplers may leak or fail in ways current local, surface-code-derived leakage/erasure schemes were not designed to detect or decode around
gaps.entry_point: Simulate leakage/erasure channels on a long-range-coupler qLDPC syndrome-extraction circuit and test whether existing removal/conversion techniques still apply
