works.what: PRX Quantum tutorial (2025) on characterization, verification and validation, led from Berkeley Lab and UC Berkeley with Sandia's Quantum Performance Laboratory: error models, tomography, randomized benchmarking and holistic benchmarks.

QSA's renewed charter targets 1,000-fold gains in computational power by 2030 through larger neutral-atom arrays (200+ qubit quantum simulators so far), trapped-ion encodings and improved superconducting control and error correction.
NERSC's IBM Quantum Innovation Center (January 2025) gives approved NERSC users cloud access to IBM quantum systems, with training and support for running algorithms.

labs.name: Oak Ridge (QSC, OLCF)
labs.focus: Validation of quantum simulations against neutron-scattering data, user access to commercial quantum hardware, and quantum-HPC integration.
labs.summary: Oak Ridge contributes on the validation and integration side. Its Quantum Science Center (renewed November 2025) is described as building open-source software for quantum-classical workflows; the OLCF Quantum Computing User Program gives merit-reviewed access to IBM, IQM, IonQ and Quantinuum hardware with hybrid allocations; and ORNL hosts on-site quantum systems and the openQSE quantum-HPC software effort. A March 2026 preprint benchmarks IBM Heron simulations against neutron-scattering data from KCuF3, an example of validating pre-fault-tolerant science (bridge milestone, P02). ORNL's Travis Humble also co-authored the 2025 certified-randomness experiment, whose classical verification used ORNL's Frontier and Summit at full-machine scale.
programs: Quantum Science Center (QSC), ORNL-led DOE National QIS Research Center, renewed Nov 2025 (focus: open-source software for quantum-classical workflows)
access: OLCF Quantum Computing User Program (apply through OLCF; open to national labs, universities, government and industry): https://www.olcf.ornl.gov/olcf-resources/compute-systems/quantum-computing-user-program/

works.what: IBM Heron processors (up to 50 qubits) compute dynamical structure factors for KCuF3 and an XXZ chain and are scored against inelastic neutron-scattering spectra with MSE, Wasserstein distance, SSIM, quantum Fisher information and two-tangle metrics.

ORNL runs a six-qubit Quantum Brilliance Quoll and a 20-qubit IQM Pathfinder on site and held an openQSE workshop on an open, modular quantum-HPC software ecosystem at its July 2026 user forum (184 attendees).
QCUP offers merit-reviewed access to IBM, IQM, IonQ and Quantinuum systems, with hybrid quantum-classical allocations alongside OLCF classical resources.

Certified randomness on Quantinuum's 56-qubit H2-1 (Nature, 2025), co-authored by Travis Humble of ORNL's Quantum Science Center: 71,313 bits of entropy certified, with classical verification spread across Frontier, Summit, Perlmutter and Polaris, Frontier and Summit at full-machine scale.

labs.name: Sandia
labs.focus: Open trapped-ion testbed, quantum characterization, verification and benchmarking, and fault-tolerant resource estimation for mission science.
labs.summary: Sandia contributes testbeds and characterization science. QSCOUT is an open trapped-ion testbed (six Yb-171 qubits, all-to-all connectivity, entangling-gate fidelities of 0.95 to 0.99) programmed in Jaqal; its page says the program ends with fiscal 2026 after DOE funding was redirected. Sandia's Quantum Performance Laboratory supplies pyGSTi and co-wrote a 2025 Nature Reviews Physics review of benchmarking, relevant to logical-level benchmarks (P15) and V&V. With Google Quantum AI, Sandia produced a 2024 fault-tolerant algorithm for fusion-relevant stopping power (P14, workflow milestone). DOE's 2026 V&V testbed call requires an Office of Science laboratory lead, so Sandia, an NNSA laboratory, can join a team but not lead one.
programs: QSCOUT (Quantum Scientific Computing Open User Testbed), trapped-ion testbed
Quantum Performance Laboratory (QPL): gate set tomography, pyGSTi, benchmarking
access: QSCOUT whitepaper-based user access (contact qscout@sandia.gov first; wind-down by end of FY2026): https://www.sandia.gov/quantum/quantum-information-sciences/projects/qscout/
pyGSTi (gate set tomography toolkit; 2020 description): https://www.osti.gov/biblio/1668693
partners: Duke University (200-qubit ion trap made by Sandia, via QSA)

works.what: QSCOUT offers six Yb-171 ion qubits with all-to-all Molmer-Sorensen gates (0.95-0.99 fidelity), pulse-level access via Jaqal and open user projects; the page says the program discontinues by end of FY2026 with limited capacity left.

Fault-tolerant quantum algorithm for electronic stopping power in extreme conditions relevant to fusion; Sandia reports that classical data cut the quantum resource requirements by several orders of magnitude.

Nature Reviews Physics perspective (2025) from Sandia's Quantum Performance Laboratory on what each type of benchmark measures, from physical-level to application-level, and how poor benchmarks can impede progress.

labs.name: Los Alamos
labs.focus: Theory and architecture co-design for early fault-tolerant neutral-atom simulation.
labs.summary: Los Alamos contributes to fault tolerance mainly through architecture co-design with QuEra: Andrew Sornborger's team helped develop the Transversal STAR architecture for megaquop-scale neutral-atom simulation (arXiv 2509.18294; QuEra release of 1 June 2026). The authors report about 250x faster execution than fixed-connectivity fully fault-tolerant architectures, about 2x fewer physical qubits than fully fault-tolerant alternatives, 20-40x lower space-time cost than the previous best STAR design, and about 10,000 physical qubits at 1e-3 two-qubit error for the surface-code version, or 1,500-3,000 for a qLDPC variant. This bears on the workflow milestone and on P14 and P05. Los Alamos is also a principal partner in Oak Ridge's Quantum Science Center, leading two thrusts.
programs: Collaboration with QuEra Computing on the Transversal STAR architecture
Quantum Science Center (ORNL-led, renewed 2025), in which Los Alamos is a principal partner leading the hybrid-algorithms and scientific-applications thrusts

works.what: Transversal STAR architecture for neutral atoms: surface-code version needs about 10,000 physical qubits at 1e-3 error for simulation volume above 600, with a qLDPC extension estimated at 1,500-3,000 physical qubits (authors' estimates).

labs.name: Lawrence Livermore (QuDIT)
labs.focus: Superconducting-qudit testbed for materials, fabrication and control co-design, with pulse-level compilation.
labs.summary: Lawrence Livermore operates the Quantum Design and Integration Testbed (QuDIT), a superconducting-processor environment for device- and system-level research on materials, fabrication, classical control and algorithms, open to LLNL researchers and their collaborators. With Rigetti, LLNL researchers used optimal-control pulses to implement arbitrary gates directly: on QuDIT's standard processor, random qutrit gates reached 97.9 ± 0.5% average fidelity, and the gates stayed robust to drift for at least three hours (Physical Review Applied, 2024). This hardware-aware compilation bears on the compiled-subroutines goal of the logic milestone and on P07, but it is not an error-correction demonstration.
access: QuDIT is available to LLNL researchers and their collaborators (no open user program is described): https://quantum.llnl.gov/research
partners: Rigetti Computing (co-authors of the 2024 qutrit pulse-compilation paper; gates also tested on Rigetti processors)

works.what: LLNL researchers use the QuDIT testbed to determine optimal materials, fabrication methods and infrastructure for superconducting qubits.

With Rigetti, optimal-control pulses implement arbitrary qutrit gates directly on LLNL's QuDIT processor at 97.9 ± 0.5% average fidelity (98.8 ± 0.6% with gate folding), instead of long sequences of primitive gates (Physical Review Applied, 2024).

labs.name: Pacific Northwest (PNNL)
labs.focus: Fault-tolerant architecture and compilation, QEC noise simulation, HPC quantum-circuit simulators and quantum-chemistry use cases.
labs.summary: Pacific Northwest National Laboratory contributes fault-tolerant architecture, compilation and noise-simulation research alongside quantum chemistry. HetEC (ASPLOS 2025, with Yale and IBM) joins surface-code and gross-code blocks through an ancilla bus, cutting physical qubits by up to 6.42x at up to 3.43x longer execution. TACO (ISCA 2026) co-designs transpiler and architecture to cut fault-tolerant execution time by up to 21.9x (mean 4.4x) against a state-of-the-art baseline, and a 2026 Physical Review Research paper models thermal-relaxation noise for stabilizer-based QEC simulation. A PNNL-led perspective (JCTC 2025) identifies chemistry use cases for machines with 25-100 logical qubits. PNNL also maintains the NWQ-Sim HPC simulators. All of this is theory, simulation or software.
programs: TEC4 (Transferring Exascale Computational Chemistry to Cloud Computing Environment and Emerging Hardware Technologies), a DOE-funded collaboration with Microsoft and Micron announced in September 2023 and led by PNNL's Karol Kowalski; it uses Azure Quantum Elements AI-augmented simulation workflows and Micron memory for classical computational chemistry
access: NWQ-Sim, PNNL's open-source state-vector (SV-Sim) and density-matrix (DM-Sim) simulators for CPU/GPU HPC systems, with Qiskit, QASM, QIR and XACC front ends: https://github.com/pnnl/NWQ-Sim
QASMBench OpenQASM benchmark suite (ACM Transactions on Quantum Computing, 2023): https://github.com/pnnl/QASMBench
partners: Yale University and IBM Quantum (HetEC co-authors, ASPLOS 2025)

works.what: Joins surface-code and gross-code blocks through an ancilla bus, cutting physical qubits by up to 6.42x at a target logical error rate at the cost of up to 3.43x longer execution, in simulation (PNNL with Yale and IBM).
TACO co-designs Clifford-reducing transpilation and the fault-tolerant architecture, cutting simulated execution time by up to 21.9x (mean 4.4x) against a state-of-the-art baseline.

PNNL-led perspective on chemistry use cases for early fault-tolerant machines with 25-100 logical qubits; modest active spaces such as Fe2S2 clusters or chromophores map to 25-40 logical qubits at depth 10^4-10^5.

QuIRC, a routing card for lattice surgery between surface-code modules on separate chips in one refrigerator, co-authored by PNNL's Ang Li with Princeton and UMass Amherst: ancilla patch size down by up to 77.8% against a single chip.

labs.name: NIST / JILA
labs.focus: Fault-tolerance theory and neutral-atom experiments through QuICS (NIST with the University of Maryland) and JILA (NIST with the University of Colorado).
labs.summary: NIST and JILA are not DOE laboratories; their fault-tolerance work appears through QuICS, NIST's joint center with the University of Maryland, and JILA, its joint institute with the University of Colorado. QuICS's Michael Gullans co-authored Harvard's 48-logical-qubit processor (Nature 2024) and the 448-atom architecture paper (Nature, November 2025), which reported 2.14(13)x below-threshold surface-code performance. QuICS researchers also led a 2D-local implementation of the [[144,12,12]] gross code using 576 qubits (PRX Quantum 2025). At JILA, Adam Kaufman's group demonstrated mid-circuit measurement and reset in a 48-site ytterbium atom array (Physical Review X 2023), a building block for repeated syndrome extraction.
programs: Joint Center for Quantum Information and Computer Science (QuICS), NIST and University of Maryland
partners: Harvard University, MIT and QuEra Computing (co-authors with QuICS on the 2024 and 2025 neutral-atom logical-processor papers)

works.what: Neutral-atom architecture on up to 448 atoms, co-authored by Michael Gullans of QuICS (NIST/University of Maryland): 2.14(13)x below-threshold surface-code performance in a four-round circuit using atom-loss detection and machine-learning decoding (Nature, November 2025).
Co-authored by QuICS's Michael Gullans: up to 48 logical qubits on up to 280 physical qubits, with 228 logical two-qubit gates and 48 logical CCZ gates.

JILA demonstrated mid-circuit measurement and reset in a 48-site ytterbium-171 array, with raw mid-circuit measurement errors of 1.8(6)% on ancilla and 4.5(1.0)% on data qubits, a building block for repeated syndrome extraction.

universities.name: Harvard University
universities.groups: Lukin and Greiner groups; Harvard-MIT Center for Ultracold Atoms
universities.focus: Neutral-atom logical processors, transversal-gate decoding, magic states, atom-array interconnects
universities.summary: Harvard's Lukin and Greiner groups, working with MIT in the Harvard-MIT Center for Ultracold Atoms, lead academic neutral-atom fault tolerance. Since 2024 they have shown a logical processor with 48 logical qubits, a 448-atom architecture combining below-threshold surface-code operation with universal logic by transversal teleportation (Nature 2025), logical magic-state distillation with colour codes, correlated decoding for transversal gates, and continuous operation of a roughly 3,000-atom array for over two hours. Much of this is done with or alongside QuEra, so attribution overlaps with that company, and several results use post-selection or small codes.
ties: AWS Center for Quantum Networking (Knaut et al., Nature 2024)

works.what: Logical processor with 48 logical qubits in [[8,3,2]] blocks, 228 logical two-qubit gates and 48 CCZ gates on up to 280 physical qubits.
Experimental logical magic-state distillation: distilled output states showed improved fidelity over inputs using d=3 and d=5 colour codes.
Correlated decoding of logical algorithms with transversal gates reduced logical error against independent per-patch decoding in simulation; a faster variant followed in 2025 (arXiv 2505.13587).

Magic tricycles: efficient magic-state generation with finite-block-length qLDPC codes, logical error at most 6e-10 with modest post-selection on 50-100-qubit codes and circuit-noise threshold above 0.5%.
Continuous coherent operation of a roughly 3,000-atom system for over two hours, addressing atom loss through reloading.

Architecture on up to 448 neutral atoms: below-threshold surface-code operation (2.14(13)x in a four-round circuit, with machine-learning decoding and atom-loss detection), universal logic by transversal teleportation with 3D codes, and mid-circuit qubit reuse that raised cycle rates by two orders of magnitude.

universities.name: MIT
universities.groups: MIT QEC and decoding groups; Harvard-MIT Center for Ultracold Atoms (atom-array interconnects)
universities.focus: qLDPC logical measurement (extractors), machine-learning decoders, optical links for atom arrays, atom-array compilation
universities.summary: MIT groups contribute decoders, logical-processing architectures and atom-array interconnect theory. Machine-learning decoders for bivariate bicycle codes (Quantum, 2026), the extractor construction for Pauli-based computation on qLDPC codes (with IBM, Oxford and Sydney) and its hypergraph-product follow-up (extractors 47-80% of base-code size) address logical operations on qLDPC memories. MIT and Harvard papers analyse fault-tolerant optical links that tolerate non-local Bell-pair errors near 10%, and Atomique targets compilation for reconfigurable atom arrays. Most results are simulations rather than hardware demonstrations.

works.what: Extractors give one logical cycle of O(d) syndrome rounds per measurement with extractor overhead of O-tilde(n) for an n-qubit qLDPC code.
Full extractors for hypergraph product codes: extractor size 47-80% of the base code, maximum qubit degree 10, and about 1e-6 measurement error at d=10 and p=1e-3.

Recurrent transformer decoder for bivariate bicycle codes under circuit-level noise (Quantum, 2026): on [[72,12,6]] at p = 0.1%, logical error almost 5x below BP-OSD and an order of magnitude faster than worst-case BP-OSD.
Error-corrected qubits can be connected by noisy links, tolerating roughly 14x higher error at the module interface than in the bulk (about 10% against 1%).
Fault-tolerant optical interconnects for neutral-atom arrays: fault tolerance achievable with local Rydberg-gate error below 1% and non-local Bell-pair error below 10%, at QEC cycles of 25-2000 kHz.
Atomique quantum compiler for reconfigurable neutral-atom arrays reports gate-count and fidelity-estimate improvements over fixed-connectivity compilation baselines.

universities.name: Caltech
universities.groups: IQIM (Preskill, Endres and collaborators); Chan group
universities.focus: qLDPC processor design, high-rate surgery, resource estimates for early fault tolerance, classical baselines
universities.summary: Caltech's IQIM combines theory leadership with neutral-atom hardware and classical-simulation baselines. The 2025-26 outputs include high-rate qLDPC processor designs with the spin-out Oratomic, where a [[540,108,18]] code reaches about 1e10 simulated logical operations with two failures, high-rate code surgery with UChicago, a resource estimate for Shor's algorithm on about 10,000 reconfigurable atoms, and the megaquop-machine framing for early fault tolerance. Caltech researchers also appear on AWS's Ocelot chip, and the Chan group's tensor-network methods challenged pre-fault-tolerance utility claims.
ties: AWS Center for Quantum Computing (Ocelot; Painter, Preskill, Brandao on the Nature paper)

works.what: High-rate qLDPC processors: [[540,108,18]] reaches about 1e10 simulated logical operations with two failures, and [[300,60,14]] about 1e-11 logical error at p=1e-3.
High-rate surgery performs hundreds of simultaneous random logical measurements at about 2x the memory space-time cost, for the gross code and codes up to 25% rate.
Resource estimate: ECC-256 with about 9,739 atomic qubits (about 264 days) and RSA-2048 with about 11,033 qubits (about 870 days).
Frames a roughly 1e6-quop megaquop machine as the next community milestone, independent of specific hardware.
Fast, converged classical simulation reached the same accuracy as the quantum device on the same task, a rebuttal to pre-fault-tolerance utility evidence.

universities.name: Yale University
universities.groups: Yale QEC architecture researchers (Kun Liu, Shifan Xu and collaborators)
universities.focus: qLDPC magic-state distillation and injection, qLDPC routing on programmable toric hardware
universities.summary: Yale researchers, including Kun Liu and Shifan Xu, study how qLDPC codes could run on programmable hardware. Their 2026 papers cover magic-state distillation in the bicycle (gross-code) architecture at space-time volume comparable to leading surface-code factories, simultaneous in-situ magic-state injection on arbitrary CSS qLDPC codes, and routing of qLDPC codes on 2D toric architectures that reduces long-range couplers from O(n) to O(sqrt n). Yale also appears among the co-authors of QuEra-led transversal fault-tolerance work. The results are simulation-based.
ties: QuEra Computing, Harvard, AWS and Caltech (co-authors with Yale's Aleksander Kubica on the Nature 2025 transversal fault-tolerance paper)
Pacific Northwest National Laboratory and IBM Quantum (HetEC co-authors, ASPLOS 2025)

works.what: Distilling magic states in the bicycle architecture reaches space-time volume comparable to leading surface-code factories at lower target error and smaller qubit footprint.
In-situ simultaneous magic-state injection on arbitrary CSS qLDPC codes: injection error 1.62e-3 per logical qubit at 1e-3 depolarizing noise, shown on [[144,12,12]] and [[225,9,4]].
Efficient routing of qLDPC codes on programmable 2D toric architectures reduces long-range couplers from O(n) to O(sqrt n); simulated 3.06% per logical qubit per cycle for [[18,4,4]].

universities.name: University of Chicago
universities.focus: Decoder scheduling, qLDPC memory architectures, high-rate surgery, verification of FT programs
universities.summary: Chicago's computer-architecture and theory groups focus on making fault-tolerant programs run efficiently. Contributions include speculative window decoding (SWIPER, ISCA 2025), which cut simulated application runtimes by 40% on average against earlier parallel window decoders, systolic atom-array movement for qLDPC memories (qSIEVE), high-rate surgery with Caltech performing hundreds of simultaneous logical measurements at about 2x memory cost, and homological-product-code computation with QuEra and Harvard. Chicago was also a partner in IBM's 2026 doped-Clifford sampling advantage demonstration and published a method for verifying programs with few T gates.

works.what: SWIPER (ISCA 2025, with the University of Michigan): speculative window decoding cuts simulated program runtimes by 40% on average against earlier parallel window decoders, at the cost of 31% more concurrent decoders.
qSIEVE co-designs a qLDPC memory with systolic atom movement and evaluates it in a hybrid qLDPC-memory and surface-code architecture.
Homological product codes give GHZ preparation with O(1) space overhead in O(1) logical cycles and magic teleportation in O(sqrt(k) log k) cycles.
High-rate surgery with Caltech: hundreds of simultaneous random logical measurements at about 2x the memory space-time cost.
With IBM, doped Clifford-circuit sampling advantage demonstration with a fidelity lower bound of 0.284 (95% CI) from 2,051 accepted samples out of about 3.5 million shots.
Lightweight, automation-friendly proofs verifying Toffoli decompositions, graph-state generators and the seven-qubit Steane encoder for programs with few T gates.

universities.name: University of Maryland (QuICS / JQI / computer science)
universities.groups: QuICS; Xiaodi Wu group; verified-software researchers
universities.focus: 2D-local qLDPC implementations, quantum control hardware, formally verified quantum software
universities.summary: At the University of Maryland, contributions span code implementation, control hardware and verified software. Berthusen et al. showed a 2D-local implementation of the [[144,12,12]] gross code with 576 qubits and 1.56e-4 logical error against 852 qubits for a comparable surface code. Xiaodi Wu's group built RISC-Q, an open generator of RISC-V-programmable control systems-on-chip (DAC 2026), and on it an open-source QEC system with 446 ns decoding-feedback latency at distance 3 in loopback tests (IEEE QCE 2026). Maryland researchers also produced the first formally certified end-to-end implementation of Shor's algorithm and verified optimisers and oracle compilers, and QuICS co-authored Harvard's logical processor. Most results are simulations, software proofs or control-hardware prototypes.
ties: QuEra Computing and Harvard (NIST/UMD co-authors of the logical processor)

works.what: 2D-local implementation of qLDPC codes: [[144,12,12]] reaches 1.56e-4 logical error with 576 qubits against 852 for a comparable surface code.

RISC-Q (DAC 2026) generates quantum-control systems-on-chip that are programmed in C, C++ or Rust through the RISC-V toolchain; its RFSoC prototype runs at 500 MHz with 16 DACs and 8 ADCs, on par with QICK and QubiC, from about a quarter of QubiC's HDL code.

Open-source QEC system built on RISC-Q and AMD ZCU216 RFSoC boards: 446 ns end-to-end decoding-feedback latency at distance 3 in loopback tests, with sub-microsecond latency projected to distance 21 (IEEE QCE 2026).
First fully formally certified end-to-end implementation of Shor's factorisation algorithm, an algorithm-level rather than gate-level proof.
Qafny type-guided proof system verifies Grover's, Shor's and quantum-walk algorithms with Coq-checked soundness (with Iowa State).
Verified compilation of quantum oracles, including a ChaCha20 cipher oracle, with performance matching Quipper.

universities.name: University of Oxford
universities.groups: Code-surgery and ion-network groups (Cowtan; Lucas group)
universities.focus: qLDPC logical measurement and surgery, distributed ion-trap computation, ZX-calculus compilation
universities.summary: Oxford's quantum code groups, with Sydney, MIT and IBM collaborators, develop logical-measurement and surgery methods for qLDPC codes. SSIP automated surgery performs half of the single-qubit logical measurements on [[144,12,12]] with 30 extra qubits against an earlier estimate of 1,380, while parallel logical measurements (PRX Quantum 2026) and auxiliary-hypergraph surgery remove the O(d)-round requirement in amortised form. Oxford's ion-trap group teleported a CZ gate between two modules over an optical link with 86.2% fidelity (Nature 2025). ZX-calculus work underpins surgery compilation.
ties: Quantinuum (SSIP author Alexander Cowtan is affiliated with both Oxford and Quantinuum)

works.what: SSIP automated surgery with qLDPC codes performs half of the single-qubit logical measurements on [[144,12,12]] with 30 extra qubits against 1,380 estimated earlier.
Framework for measuring multiple logical Pauli operators in parallel by code surgery on qLDPC codes (with IBM, Sydney and MIT).
Auxiliary hypergraphs and transversal surgery remove the O(d)-round requirement in amortised form and prove circuit equivalence with homomorphic measurement.
Distributed quantum computing across an optical network link: teleported CZ gate fidelity 86.2(9)%, entanglement rate 9.7 per second at 96.89(8)% Bell fidelity, and Grover success 71(1)%.
ZX calculus as a language for surface-code lattice surgery, deriving six previously unknown CNOT implementations and a more efficient T-gate lattice-surgery protocol (2017 foundation).

universities.name: University of Sydney
universities.groups: Quantum theory and QEC groups (Bartlett, Doherty, Harper)
universities.focus: qLDPC logic with long-range connectivity, noise learning from syndromes, noise-aware decoding, magic-state cultivation
universities.summary: The University of Sydney's quantum theory groups work on qLDPC logic and on noise learning for error correction. Cohen et al. showed an order-of-magnitude overhead reduction using long-range connectivity at about 100 logical qubits, and Sydney co-authored the extractor and parallel-measurement surgery papers. Harper, Hockings and Doherty developed scalable noise characterisation of syndrome-extraction circuits and noise-aware decoding that improved logical error suppression, and earlier work learned correlated noise on a 39-qubit processor to about 0.1% relative error. Most results are simulation or small-device characterisation rather than logical-qubit demonstrations.

works.what: Low-overhead fault tolerance with long-range connectivity: order-of-magnitude overhead reduction against the surface code at about 100 logical qubits, using a few thousand physical qubits.
Scalable noise characterisation of syndrome-extraction circuits with averaged circuit eigenvalue sampling, with polynomial scaling for QEC-relevant circuits.
Noise-aware decoding improves logical error suppression against noise-agnostic decoding.
Built noise models from syndromes of 20 data qubits on a 39-qubit processor, reaching about 0.1% relative error.

Efficient magic-state cultivation on the surface code with Hebrew University: generation rate improved more than 20x under realistic noise, and infidelity below 1e-6 using only nine physical erasure qubits.

universities.name: TU Delft / QuTech
universities.groups: Terhal group and QuTech quantum-network researchers
universities.focus: Code-hardware co-design for bivariate bicycle codes, distributed surface-code thresholds, adaptive decoding
universities.summary: TU Delft and QuTech contribute code-hardware co-design and thresholds for distributed error correction. Morphing circuits by Shaw and Terhal lower the qubit degree of bivariate bicycle codes from 6 to 5 while preserving performance, easing the connectivity burden of IBM's gross-code approach. De Bone et al. found distributed surface codes need an entanglement-generation to memory-decoherence rate ratio of about 400, roughly 3x stricter than earlier estimates. Earlier Delft work on adaptive decoder weights tracked drifting error rates in simulation. The results are theory and simulation rather than experiments.
ties: Qblox (QuTech spin-off supplying qubit control electronics; closed a real-time QEC loop with Riverlane's decoder on emulated measurement data in 2026)

works.what: Morphing circuits lower the connectivity needed for bivariate bicycle codes to qubit degree 5 instead of 6 while preserving performance.
Thresholds for the distributed surface code under memory decoherence require an entanglement-generation to decoherence rate ratio of about 400, roughly 3x stricter than earlier estimates.
Adaptive weight estimator tracks slowly drifting error rates better than static decoder weights in simulation (2018 foundation).

universities.name: ETH Zurich
universities.focus: Experimentally informed decoding, microwave module links, realistic advantage and chemistry estimates
universities.summary: ETH Zurich contributes experimental decoding, lattice surgery, module links and application-level realism. Remm et al. (2025) built decoders informed by measured syndrome correlations rather than assumed noise. Besedin et al. (Nature Physics 2026) performed lattice surgery on a 17-qubit device, splitting a distance-3 surface-code qubit into two distance-3 repetition-code qubits; the decoded logical ZZ value reached 0.730(3) against 0.591(8) for a comparable unencoded circuit. Magnard et al. linked superconducting circuits in separate cryostats over a 5 m cryogenic channel with 79.5% remote entanglement fidelity. Hoefler and colleagues argued for judging advantage by realistic runtime and energy, and Reiher's group estimated what nitrogenase chemistry would need.

works.what: Experimentally informed decoding of stabiliser codes uses measured syndrome correlation structure rather than assumed noise, improving decoding.
Microwave quantum link between superconducting circuits in separate cryostats: state-transfer fidelity 85.8% and remote two-qubit entanglement fidelity 79.5% across a 5 m cryogenic link.
Recommends judging quantum advantage by actual physical run-time and energy cost rather than asymptotic query complexity alone.
First detailed resource estimate showing quantum simulation of nitrogenase active-site reaction mechanisms is feasible at moderate qubit counts (2017).

Lattice surgery on a 17-qubit device splits a distance-3 surface-code qubit into two distance-3 repetition-code qubits; the decoded logical ZZ value reaches 0.730(3) against 0.591(8) for a comparable unencoded circuit.

universities.name: Tsinghua University
universities.groups: Quantum-code and compilation researchers (including Zi-Wen Liu's group)
universities.focus: Hardware-aware qLDPC code design, low-weight codes, routing with expanded instruction sets
universities.summary: Tsinghua groups work on hardware-aware qLDPC code design. Louvre routes bivariate bicycle codes with an expanded instruction set, cutting average qubit degree from 6 to 4.5 (or 4) at similar error. Wei et al. derived exact optimal weights for low-weight codes up to n of 9 and applied them to IBM's 127-qubit Eagle layout. He and Liu (UT Austin and Tsinghua) used reinforcement learning to find weight-6 codes with one to two orders of magnitude lower qubit overhead than earlier results. These are code-design and simulation results; Tsinghua's Dong-Ling Deng is also a corresponding author of Zhejiang University's 2026 hardware test of bivariate bicycle codes.

works.what: Louvre relaxes hardware requirements of qLDPC codes: average qubit degree 4.5 (Louvre-7) or 4 (Louvre-8) against 6 for bivariate bicycle codes, with indistinguishable error at the same depth for Louvre-7.
Theory of low-weight quantum codes with exact optimal weights for all parameters with n up to 9, and an IBM 127-qubit Eagle case study.
Reinforcement-learning discovery of low-weight codes with one to two orders of magnitude lower physical-qubit overhead than prior weight-6 results.

universities.name: UCLA
universities.focus: Compilers for neutral-atom and fault-tolerant machines; lattice-surgery synthesis; reinforcement learning for syndrome extraction
universities.summary: UCLA's VAST Lab builds compilers for neutral-atom and fault-tolerant machines. Its 2024 near-optimal scheduler for field-programmable qubit arrays gives 3.7x fewer gate stages and 5.9x estimated fidelity improvement over OLSQ-DPQA and scales to 10,000 qubits in 30 minutes, reuse-aware zoned compilation (HPCA 2025) cuts atom moves and depth, and a SAT-based lattice-surgery synthesis tool built with Google and UCSB found an 8% smaller 15-to-1 T-factory than a human design. A separate UCLA group (Palsberg) applied reinforcement learning to syndrome-extraction scheduling in 2026, cutting simulated logical error against earlier automatic schedulers.
ties: Google Quantum AI and UCSB (SAT scalpel)

works.what: Provably near-optimal scheduling for dynamically field-programmable qubit arrays: 3.7x fewer gate stages and 5.9x estimated fidelity improvement over OLSQ-DPQA, scaling to 10,000 qubits in 30 minutes.
Reuse-aware compilation for zoned neutral-atom architectures reduces atom-move count and circuit depth against non-reuse-aware zoned compilers.
SAT scalpel for lattice surgery (with Google and UCSB): 8% smaller 15-to-1 T-factory than the human design and 56% average space-time volume reduction on 101 graph-state benchmarks.
Established the OLSQ-DPQA compilation baseline against which later near-optimal neutral-atom schedulers are benchmarked.

FastSched schedules syndrome extraction with reinforcement learning: logical error 25.9% and 71.7% lower on average than AlphaSyndrome and PropHunt, and 97.8% lower than AlphaSyndrome for a distance-15 surface code (simulation).

universities.name: UC Berkeley
universities.focus: Transversal non-Clifford qLDPC codes, early fault-tolerant algorithms, classical baselines
universities.summary: UC Berkeley contributes theory spanning codes and early fault-tolerant algorithms. Golowich and Guruswami (STOC 2025) built qLDPC codes with transversal non-Clifford gates from products of algebraic codes, with distance at least N^(1/r)/polylog(N) and dimension at least N^(1-epsilon), supporting distillation with arbitrarily small yield parameter. Lin Lin and Yu Tong gave Heisenberg-limited ground-state energy estimation and state preparation for early fault-tolerant computers with reduced circuit depth. Berkeley also took part in Google's NMR companion test and the Oratomic Shor resource estimate.

works.what: qLDPC codes with transversal non-Clifford gates from products of algebraic codes: distance D at least N^(1/r)/polylog(N), dimension K at least N^(1-epsilon), supporting distillation with arbitrarily small yield parameter.
Heisenberg-limited ground-state energy estimation for early fault-tolerant computers, with optimal total-repetition scaling without full phase-estimation depth.
Ground-state preparation and energy estimation via quantum eigenvalue transformation of unitary matrices, reducing circuit depth against standard phase estimation.
With Google, constructive-interference (quantum echoes) experiment about 13,000x faster than an estimated Frontier run; the companion NMR test was explicitly not yet beyond classical.

universities.name: Zhejiang University and USTC
universities.groups: Zhejiang University superconducting-processor group; USTC Zuchongzhi team
universities.focus: Experimental QEC on superconducting processors: low-overhead codes, leakage suppression, below-threshold surface code
universities.summary: Chinese superconducting-qubit groups have reported hardware error correction with both high-rate and surface codes. A Zhejiang University-led team with Tsinghua co-authors (Wang et al., Nature Physics 2026) ran two qLDPC codes on a 32-qubit processor with long-range couplers: an [[18,4,4]] bivariate bicycle code at 8.91(17)% error per logical qubit per cycle and an [[18,6,3]] code with six logical qubits at 7.77(12)%. USTC's Zuchongzhi 3.2 team operated a distance-7 surface code on 97 qubits below threshold, with a net error-suppression factor of about 1.4 as code distance grew, using all-microwave leakage suppression (Physical Review Letters, December 2025).
ties: Tsinghua University (co-authors of the Zhejiang qLDPC experiment, including corresponding author Dong-Ling Deng)

works.what: Hardware demonstration of a low-overhead [[18,4,4]] code at 8.91(17)% error per logical qubit per cycle on a superconducting processor.
Six-logical-qubit distance-3 code at 7.77(12)% error per logical qubit per cycle, from the same low-overhead-code experiment.

Zuchongzhi 3.2 runs a distance-7 surface code on 97 qubits below threshold, with error-suppression factor 1.4, using all-microwave leakage suppression in every cycle (Physical Review Letters, December 2025).

companies.name: Quantinuum
companies.focus: Trapped-ion QCCD hardware; logical qubits, logical non-Clifford gates, GPU decoding
companies.summary: Quantinuum builds trapped-ion QCCD machines (H1, H2, Helios) and has one of the broadest logical-qubit records outside the big four. With Microsoft it showed repeated error correction with better-than-physical logical error rates (2024), with Colorado it entangled four logical qubits in a non-local code beyond break-even, and in 2025 it reported a high-fidelity logical non-Clifford gate. In February 2026 (arXiv 2602.22211) the 98-qubit Helios ran 48 error-corrected and up to 94 error-detected logical qubits using iceberg and concatenated iceberg codes. Most results are vendor-reported, and several rely on post-selection or error detection rather than full correction.

works.what: Helios (98 qubits) ran between 48 and 94 logical qubits with iceberg [[k+2,k,2]] error-detecting codes and concatenated iceberg error-correcting codes; Quantinuum's blog adds 48 error-corrected and up to 94 error-detected logical qubits, a 94-logical-qubit GHZ state at 94.9% fidelity and logical beating physical by up to 10-100x (vendor-reported; error detection and post-selection for the largest runs).
Entangled four logical qubits in a non-local code with logical GHZ fidelity 99.5-99.7% against 97.8-98.7% for the unencoded physical GHZ state.
Tesseract-code experiment (with Microsoft) prepared graph states on up to 12 logical qubits over five error-correction rounds with about 10x lower error than unencoded circuits.

Logical controlled-Hadamard non-Clifford gate on the 20-qubit H1-1 with logical infidelity at most 2.3e-4 against 1e-3 for the physical gate, and a magic state with infidelity 7e-5 at 14.8% discard (post-selected).
Joint repeated-error-correction experiment with Microsoft: logical error 9.8x-500x lower than physical with the [[7,1,3]] code and 4.7x-800x lower with the [[12,2,4]] code.
With JPMorganChase and DOE labs, certified 71,313 bits of entropy from a 56-qubit H2 run, with classical verification costing 1.1 ExaFLOPS aggregate compute.

companies.name: Microsoft (with Atom Computing)
companies.focus: Qubit virtualisation, codes and resource estimation; partner hardware from Quantinuum and Atom Computing
companies.summary: Microsoft supplies qubit-virtualisation software, error-correcting codes and resource-estimation tools, and pairs them with partner hardware. With Quantinuum it reported better-than-physical logical qubits and a tesseract-code experiment on H2 (2024). With Atom Computing it entangled 24 logical qubits built from 48 neutral ytterbium atoms and ran a Bernstein-Vazirani circuit on up to 28 logical qubits using 112 atoms, correcting on average 1.8 lost atoms through erasure conversion (arXiv 2411.11822). The Azure Quantum Resource Estimator is a widely used fault-tolerance cost tool. The planned Danish Magne machine is a plan, not a demonstration.

works.what: With Atom Computing, entangled 24 logical qubits made from 48 neutral Yb atoms and ran an algorithm on up to 28 logical qubits (112 atoms), correcting on average 1.8 lost atoms with erasure conversion; logical error rates were better than physical.
Joint experiment on Quantinuum H2 showing repeated error correction with logical error rates 4.7x-800x below physical, depending on the code (vendor-reported).
Tesseract-code demonstration of logical computation and repeated error correction on up to 12 logical qubits, with about 10x lower error than unencoded circuits.
Azure Quantum Resource Estimator evaluates logical and physical resources automatically, shown on three distinct multiplication algorithms.
Methodology paper on the requirements for practical quantum advantage that underlies the later Azure Quantum Resource Estimator.
Polynomial-time routing algorithm for surface-code compilation, proven near-optimal in circuit depth for broad classes of lattice-surgery instances.

companies.name: Amazon / AWS Center for Quantum Computing
companies.focus: Cat qubits and bosonic codes, dual-rail erasure qubits, end-to-end algorithm resource surveys
companies.summary: AWS Center for Quantum Computing, working with Caltech, pursues hardware-efficient fault tolerance with bosonic and erasure qubits. Its Ocelot chip (Nature, 2025) concatenated cat qubits with an outer repetition code at distances 3 and 5; the phase-flip code operated below threshold, and logical error per cycle was 1.75(2)% at d=3 and 1.65(3)% at d=5. AWS also demonstrated a long-coherence dual-rail erasure qubit on tunable transmons, co-led an end-to-end resource survey of quantum algorithms, and supports networking research with Harvard. These results are small memories rather than logical computation.

works.what: Ocelot concatenated cat qubits with an outer repetition code at distances 3 to 5; the phase-flip repetition code ran below threshold, with logical error per cycle 1.75(2)% at d=3 and 1.65(3)% at d=5.
Long-coherence dual-rail erasure qubit on tunable transmons whose dominant errors are locatable erasures rather than Pauli errors.

Flag-qubit magic-state preparation with redundant ancilla encoding, reported to need an order of magnitude fewer qubits and space-time overhead than competing distillation near p of about 1e-4 (2020 foundation).
AWS-led multi-institution survey consolidating per-algorithm resource claims into one comparable end-to-end reference for quantum applications.
Harvard and AWS Center for Quantum Networking entangled nanophotonic memory nodes (electron-spin fidelity 0.86(3), up to 1 Hz) over a 35 km deployed fibre loop.

companies.name: Riverlane
companies.focus: Real-time decoders, QEC control stack, qLDPC decoding, code design for fixed connectivity
companies.summary: Riverlane (UK) is a decoding and QEC control-stack company. Its Local Clustering Decoder, an adaptive FPGA decoder published in Nature Communications in December 2025, completes a decoding round in under one microsecond and ships in Deltaflow 2 with partners including Infleqtion, Oxford Quantum Circuits, Oak Ridge and Rigetti. Ambiguity Clustering targets qLDPC codes and is reported up to 27-150x faster than BP-OSD, and with Rigetti it showed real-time decoding on superconducting hardware. With Qblox it closed a full QEC loop in 6.886 microseconds for a Surface-17 code using emulated measurement data. Most figures are company-reported, and the qLDPC decoding work is simulation.

works.what: Ambiguity Clustering decoder for qLDPC codes, reported up to 27-150x faster than the BP-OSD baseline.
Parallel window decoding shows decoding without backlog growth as lattice size grows, in simulation.
With Rigetti, real-time low-latency decoding on superconducting qubits: mean decode time under 1 microsecond per round and 9.6 microsecond response time over nine rounds.
Qblox and Riverlane closed a full real-time QEC loop at 6.886 microseconds on Surface-17 and under 12 microseconds on Surface-161 (company announcement).
Directional codes match rotated toric-code logical error at p=1e-3 with one quarter to one third of the physical qubits on hexagonal and square-grid connectivity.

Local Clustering Decoder, an adaptive FPGA hardware decoder published in Nature Communications, completes one decoding round in under one microsecond; the Deltaflow 2 system that includes it is deployed with Infleqtion, Oxford Quantum Circuits, Oak Ridge National Laboratory and Rigetti (company claims).

companies.name: NVIDIA
companies.focus: GPU-QPU coupling (NVQLink), CUDA-Q QEC and logical-level compilation, AI for calibration and decoding
companies.summary: NVIDIA supplies the GPU side of fault tolerance and builds no qubits. Its NVQLink architecture paper reports 3.96 microseconds maximum round-trip latency between GPUs and QPUs, and the platform launched with 17 hardware builders and 9 national labs. CUDA-Q QEC and cudaq-realtime provide decoder libraries and real-time programming for a logical QPU, CUDA-Q Logical retargets one compiler front-end to more than one logical-code backend, and the April 2026 Ising models apply AI to calibration and error correction. Several cited items are software or product announcements, and results depend on partner hardware.

works.what: NVQLink architecture paper reports 3.96 microsecond maximum round-trip latency for tightly coupling HPC/GPU systems with QPUs, with LBNL, Sandia and ORNL co-authors.
CUDA-Q Logical shows one compiler front-end retargeted to more than one logical-code backend, the closest existing system to a shared cross-modality fault-tolerant intermediate representation.
CUDA-Q QEC 0.6 enables real-time QEC with NVQLink (software release announcement).
cudaq-realtime provides a programming model for the logical QPU (software announcement).
NVQLink launched with 17 quantum-hardware partners and 9 national labs signed on.
NVIDIA Ising open AI models for quantum calibration and error correction launched in April 2026 with hardware partners.

companies.name: Alice & Bob
companies.focus: Superconducting cat qubits with exponentially suppressed bit-flips; LDPC-cat codes
companies.summary: Alice & Bob (Paris) builds superconducting cat qubits whose bit-flip errors are exponentially suppressed, so error correction only needs to handle phase flips. Its LDPC-cat codes (Nature Communications 2025) combine cat qubits with qLDPC codes on a 2D-local layout, estimating 100 logical qubits at about 1e-8 logical error per cycle from a 758-qubit chip design. A company estimate puts FeMoco and P450 chemistry at roughly 99,000 cat qubits and 78 to 99 hours, about 27x fewer physical qubits than a transmon plus surface-code estimate. These are design and resource estimates, not demonstrations.

works.what: LDPC-cat codes pair cat qubits with qLDPC codes on 2D-local layouts, estimating 100 logical qubits at about 1e-8 logical error per cycle with a 758-qubit chip design.
Company estimate for quantum chemistry on cat qubits: about 99,000 cat qubits and 78 h (FeMoco) or 99 h (P450) runtime, about 27x fewer physical qubits than a transmon plus surface-code estimate.
Squeezed cat qubits: a 22 s bit-flip time at a 1.3 µs phase-flip time, 160 times longer than a standard cat qubit at the same phase-flip time (single-qubit experiment, 2025 preprint).

companies.name: PsiQuantum
companies.focus: Fusion-based photonic quantum computing on silicon photonics in a commercial foundry
companies.summary: PsiQuantum builds fusion-based photonic quantum computers on silicon photonics made on 300-mm wafers in a commercial foundry. Its 2025 Nature paper reported 99.98% state preparation and measurement fidelity, 99.50% Hong-Ou-Mandel visibility, 99.22% two-qubit fusion fidelity and 99.72% chip-to-chip qubit interconnect fidelity, the last conditional on detection and excluding loss. It also published fault-tolerant resource estimates for chemistry, showing that parallel magic-state factories cut runtime by about an order of magnitude. The Nature paper reports component fidelities, not logical qubits, and photon loss remains the central challenge.

works.what: Manufacturable silicon-photonic platform on 300-mm wafers with 99.98% SPAM, 99.50% HOM visibility, 99.22% two-qubit fusion and 99.72% chip-to-chip qubit interconnect fidelity (conditional on detection, excluding loss).
Fault-tolerant resource estimate for Li-ion battery electrolyte chemistry showing parallel magic-state factories cut runtime about tenfold at the same physical-qubit footprint for photonic FTQC.

companies.name: Infleqtion
companies.focus: Neutral-atom Sqale platform; logical qubits with loss correction; Rydberg-gate qLDPC architectures
companies.summary: Infleqtion builds neutral-atom machines (Sqale) and collaborates with Wisconsin on Rydberg-gate designs for qLDPC codes. In experiments from August 2026, announced on 24 September at the Quantum World Congress, it reported 30 logical qubits encoded in 80 physical qubits, preparing [[8,3,3]] states and then using [[8,3,2]] codes that detect errors or correct a lost atom. An IQP-circuit test gave a hit fraction near 25% against 0.024% for the baseline, about 1,000x, and loss correction in post-processing quadrupled good shots. The paper was not yet posted at announcement, and the result is error detection plus loss correction, not full error correction.

works.what: 30 logical qubits in 80 physical qubits on Sqale; an IQP-circuit test reached a hit fraction of about 25% against 0.024% for the baseline (about 1,000x), announced 24 Sep 2026 with the paper still to come.
[[8,3,2]] codes detect errors or correct a lost atom; correcting loss in post-processing quadrupled the number of good shots (error detection plus loss correction, not full error correction).
Architecture for fast qLDPC-code implementation with optimised Rydberg gates: CZ fidelity above 0.999 beyond 12 micrometres and a QEC cycle of about 1.28 ms for [[144,12,12]].

companies.name: Pasqal
companies.focus: Neutral-atom QPUs; logical-qubit benchmarks with [[4,2,2]] error detection; on-chip photonic control
companies.summary: Pasqal (France) builds neutral-atom quantum processors. In May 2026 it reported two logical qubits encoded in four physical qubits with the [[4,2,2]] error-detecting code, used to solve differential equations with a quantum-kernel algorithm across 1,000 test equations; logical results beat physical by over 50% on average and up to 10x on nonlinear problems, with Paris-Saclay and Institut d'Optique (arXiv 2605.21276). Errors were detected and post-selected, not corrected in real time. In August 2026 Pasqal reported holding four rubidium atoms in traps formed by light from a silicon-nitride photonic chip, with atom lifetimes of about 27.5 seconds (company announcement). With IBM, Pasqal proposed a framework for quantum advantage.

works.what: Two logical qubits in four physical qubits ([[4,2,2]] error-detecting code) solved 1,000 differential equations with a quantum-kernel algorithm: median residual 0.042 logical against 0.069 physical and nonlinear error 0.011 against 0.122, on a neutral-atom processor with 99.4% combined gate fidelity; errors were detected and post-selected, not corrected.
Four rubidium atoms held in optical traps formed by light from one silicon-nitride photonic chip, with atom lifetimes of about 27.5 s (company announcement, no paper).
IBM and Pasqal two-condition criterion (verifiability plus improvement) across sampling, variational and expectation-value problem classes, with a three-tier error-handling taxonomy.

companies.name: Xanadu
companies.focus: Photonic GKP qubits, modular photonic networking, logical measurement schemes
companies.summary: Xanadu (Toronto) pursues photonic quantum computing built on GKP qubits and modular networking. Its 2025 Nature papers reported an integrated photonic GKP-qubit source and the Aurora modular machine, which synthesised 86.4 billion entangled modes and ran for two hours continuously. On the theory side, its homological-measurement scheme (PRX 2025) performs logical measurements with ancillas linear in operator weight, for example 16 against 230 ancillas in simulated photonic GKP cases. These are component, networking and architecture milestones; none of the cited results reports a logical computation.

works.what: Homological measurement performs fault-tolerant logical measurements with ancillas linear in operator weight, for example 16 against 230 ancillas in simulated photonic GKP cases.
Aurora modular photonic machine synthesised 86.4 billion entangled modes, and a two-hour continuous run yielded 7.2 billion temporal modes.

On-chip source of optical GKP qubits on a 300-mm silicon-nitride platform: at least four resolvable peaks per quadrature and a 3 × 3 grid of negative Wigner regions; fault tolerance needs lower optical loss (Nature, 2025).

companies.name: Photonic Inc.
companies.focus: Spin-photon (T-centre in silicon) qubits; SHYPS qLDPC codes
companies.summary: Photonic Inc. (Vancouver) builds spin-photon qubits linked by optical connections and designs qLDPC codes for them. Its SHYPS family (Subsystem Hypergraph Product Simplex) appeared as Computing Efficiently in QLDPC Codes (arXiv February 2025) and was published in Nature Communications in May 2026, with two co-authors also at Edinburgh and FU Berlin. Any m-qubit Clifford operation takes at most O(m) syndrome-extraction rounds; in circuit-level simulation, depth-126 logical circuits reach near-memory performance, and a [[225,16,8]] SHYPS code performs comparably to a [[784,16,7]] distance-7 surface-code layout with 3.5x fewer qubits. These are code-level simulations, not hardware logical qubits.

works.what: SHYPS codes run any m-qubit Clifford in O(m) syndrome rounds; a [[225,16,8]] code performs like a distance-7 surface-code layout with 3.5x fewer qubits, and depth-126 logical circuits stay near memory performance (simulation).

companies.name: Rigetti
companies.focus: Superconducting chiplet processors; real-time decoding integration; open resource estimation
companies.summary: Rigetti (US) builds superconducting processors, and its fault-tolerance contribution is mainly decoding integration and tooling. With Riverlane it ran real-time FPGA decoding on its hardware (Nature Communications, 2026): an eight-qubit stability experiment with mean decode time under 1 microsecond per round, and a fast-feedback test with a 9.6 microsecond response time over nine rounds. These test decoding rather than a logical-qubit memory or gate. Riverlane lists Rigetti among the partners where its Deltaflow 2 hardware decoder is deployed. The open-source Rigetti Resource Estimation tool, funded by DARPA, supports parameter sweeps for fault-tolerant cost studies. In April 2026 Rigetti made its 108-qubit Cepheus-1-108Q system generally available.

works.what: With Riverlane, real-time low-latency decoding on superconducting qubits: mean decode time under 1 microsecond per round and 9.6 microsecond response time over nine rounds.
Open-source Rigetti Resource Estimation command-line tool and library with parameter-sweep support for design-space exploration of fault-tolerant costs (DARPA-funded).

Riverlane states that its Deltaflow 2 hardware-decoder system, built around the Local Clustering Decoder, is deployed with Rigetti alongside Infleqtion, Oxford Quantum Circuits and Oak Ridge National Laboratory (company claim).

companies.name: IQM
companies.focus: Superconducting processors; tile codes and hardware-aware qLDPC design
companies.summary: IQM (Finland) builds superconducting processors and, with Breuckmann Ltd and JGU Mainz, introduced tile codes, qLDPC codes designed for a 2D lattice with boundary. Reported examples include [[288,8,12]] with weight 6, [[288,8,14]] and [[512,18,19]] with weight 8; the last is reported more than 12x better than the rotated surface code. Tile codes and IQM's 2026 barbell and nearest-neighbour qLDPC codes are simulation studies. On hardware, IQM encoded two logical qubits in the [[4,2,2]] error-detecting code on a six-qubit star-topology processor (PRX Quantum), with logical error of 0.25-0.91% per cycle after post-selection. Tile codes target planar chips with only local connections.

works.what: Tile codes: [[288,8,12]] (weight 6), [[288,8,14]] and [[512,18,19]] (weight 8); the last reported more than 12x better than the rotated surface code.

programs.name: Quantum Genesis Q Competition
programs.what: Announced 2026-09-17: up to $215M planned. Phase I gives fixed milestone awards up to $1.5M per awardee; Phase II has a $100M incentive pool for systems with at least 100 logical qubits running hundreds of millions of fault-tolerant operations, plus two $50M bonus pools at 150 and 200 logical qubits. Open to private-sector companies, modality-agnostic; applications due 2026-10-19.

programs.name: Quantum HPC Validation and Verification Testbed (LAB 26-3603)
programs.what: DOE laboratory call for $45M over FY26-FY28 ($14M in FY26), 1-2 awards of $7-15M per year for 3 years. The lead must be a DOE Office of Science national laboratory, with at least two collaborators from outside the DOE/NNSA laboratory complex and any number of DOE/NNSA laboratories; LOI due 2026-09-30, proposals due 2026-11-10, awards anticipated winter 2026-27. Scope is stack-wide V&V across qubit modalities; hardware development and hybrid quantum-classical algorithm work are out of scope; tools may feed the Genesis Mission infrastructure platform and American Science Cloud.

programs.name: NQISRC renewal
programs.what: On 2025-11-04 DOE announced $625M over up to five years for C2QA (BNL), SQMS (Fermilab), Q-NEXT (Argonne), QSA (LBNL) and QSC (ORNL); $125M in FY2025, later years subject to appropriations. Each center was renewed at $125M over five years.

programs.name: SCAC Quantum Subcommittee roadmap (Sept 2026)
programs.what: Advisory-committee roadmap proposing Quantum Grand Challenges in 2026-2028, a conditional DOE Quantum Computing User Facility, and 2028 demonstration targets of 50 to 100 logical qubits and 10,000 to 100,000 hard logical operations with independent validation within 24 hours.

programs.name: OLCF Quantum Computing User Program (QCUP)
programs.what: Merit-reviewed access to IBM, IQM, IonQ and Quantinuum systems for national labs, universities, government and industry, with hybrid allocations alongside OLCF classical resources.

programs.name: QSCOUT open trapped-ion testbed (Sandia)
programs.what: DOE-funded open user testbed of six Yb-171 qubits; Sandia's page says the program discontinues by end of FY2026 due to DOE funding redirection.

programs.name: NERSC quantum access
programs.what: NERSC opened cloud access to IBM quantum computers for approved NERSC users through an IBM Quantum Innovation Center (January 2025), and its open 2026 call offered access to QuEra's Aquila analog and Gemini gate-based neutral-atom systems in two stages through December 2026.

collaborations.what: Pattern: hardware maker plus software and QEC partner. Joint 2024 experiments on H2 gave logical error rates 4.7x-800x below physical (depending on the code) and a tesseract-code demonstration on up to 12 logical qubits.

Pattern: software-defined logical qubits on a partner's neutral-atom hardware. 24 logical qubits from 48 Yb atoms, algorithms on up to 28 logical qubits (112 atoms), 1.8 lost atoms corrected on average.

Pattern: foundation and state co-funded machine. Announced July 2025 with EUR 80M: a planned machine with about 50 logical qubits and over 1,200 physical qubits, Atom Computing building the hardware and Microsoft supplying software and error correction, first tasks expected around the new year 2026/27. A plan, not a demonstration.
Pattern: QPU maker plus decoder company. Real-time low-latency decoding on superconducting qubits with mean decode time under 1 microsecond per round and 9.6 microsecond response over nine rounds.

Pattern: GPU vendor, national labs and many QPU builders around one interconnect standard. NVQLink architecture paper reports 3.96 microsecond maximum round-trip latency; the platform launched with 17 hardware partners and 9 national labs.

Pattern: corporate lab embedded with a university theory group. Ocelot concatenated cat qubits with a repetition code at distances 3 to 5 (Nature 2025); the author list includes Painter, Preskill and Brandao of Caltech.

Pattern: university spin-out publishing resource estimates and architectures. Shor's algorithm with about 10,000 reconfigurable atomic qubits (ECC-256 about 9,739 qubits), followed by high-rate qLDPC processor designs (arXiv 2607.28795).

Pattern: academic lab and spin-out company co-authoring flagship hardware papers. Logical processor with 48 logical qubits in [[8,3,2]] blocks, 228 logical two-qubit gates and 48 CCZ gates on up to 280 physical qubits.

Pattern: company plus a cluster of university code-theory groups. Extractors for Pauli-based computation on qLDPC codes (one logical cycle of O(d) rounds per measurement) and the parallel-measurement surgery follow-ups.
Pattern: hardware company with European code-theory academics. SHYPS qLDPC codes ([[225,16,8]] matching a [[784,16,7]] surface code with 3.5x fewer qubits, authors' simulation figures).

Pattern: hardware company plus a code-design consultancy and a university. Tile codes for 2D lattices with boundary, for example [[512,18,19]] reported more than 12x better than the rotated surface code.
Pattern: hardware company, bank and DOE labs. Certified randomness from a 56-qubit H2 run, 71,313 bits, with classical verification on 1.1 ExaFLOPS aggregate compute.

Pattern: a vendor-neutral decoder company deployed across several QPU makers and a DOE lab. Riverlane states its Deltaflow 2 hardware decoder (Local Clustering Decoder, under 1 microsecond per round on FPGA) is deployed with these partners (company claim).

Pattern: company plus French universities under a national programme. Two logical qubits in four physical qubits ([[4,2,2]] error detection) solved differential equations, with logical results beating physical by over 50% on average; errors were post-selected, not corrected (40 authors, arXiv 2605.21276).

notes: Coverage: work from 2023 to September 2026 that bears on fault-tolerant quantum computing, plus a few earlier foundational papers marked with their year. Profiles reflect public sources as of 1 October 2026.

Evidence levels: E0, announced (press or roadmap statement, no technical paper); E1, theory, analysis, resource estimates or simulation; E2, small-scale, offline or post-selected hardware; E3, hardware at roadmap-relevant scale with public data.

Tools and programs (software, testbeds, user facilities) and reviews are labeled separately from evidence levels. Figures from company announcements or company-run experiments without independent reproduction are labeled company-reported or vendor-reported.
A co-authored work is credited to every laboratory, university and company named on it, so one paper can appear in several profiles.
Harvard and MIT work co-authored with QuEra, one of the four roadmap companies, is listed under those universities, with QuEra named under ties.

DOE's 2026 calls: the Q Competition is open to private companies, and the V&V testbed call needs an Office of Science laboratory lead with outside collaborators. No awards had been announced by 1 October 2026.

heroes.title: Modular machines built on high-rate codes
heroes.text: IBM plans fault tolerance on bivariate-bicycle codes across linked superconducting modules: Starling in 2029 with 200 logical qubits and 10⁸ gates, then Blue Jay in 2033 with 2,000.

heroes.title: Prove each layer of error correction, then scale
heroes.text: Google's six milestones are defined by logical error rates rather than dates. Willow ran a surface-code memory below threshold, and reinforcement-learning control lowered its error to 0.077% per cycle in 2026.

heroes.title: Move the atoms, compute with transversal logic
heroes.text: QuEra moves atoms for all-to-all connectivity and transversal logical gates. It targets Libra in 2028, with over 256 logical qubits at 10⁻⁶ error on Amazon Braket, and a gigaquop system with over 1,000 logical qubits in 2028–29.

heroes.title: Electronic qubit control on a manufacturable chip
heroes.text: IonQ's dates are the most aggressive: about 800 logical qubits on a 10,000-qubit chip in 2027 and up to 80,000 logical qubits by 2030. Its public hardware shows a post-selected qLDPC memory at breakeven on 40 ions.
